title: We the People
location: Studio Montclair, 127 Bloomfield Avenue, Montclair, NJ, 07042, United States
description:
Studio Montclair (SMI) is privileged to present “We the People,” a timely exploration of expansive visual interpretations of our country’s 250-year-old experiment in democracy. We the People will run from September 18 through October 23 at SMI’s Leach Gallery, 641 Bloomfield Avenue, Montclair, NJ. An opening reception will be held on Friday, September 18 from 6:00-8:00pm. 
The opening words of the US Constitution’s Preamble outlining the Constitution’s goals and justification, “We the People,” affirms that the US government serves its citizens and that the people are the ultimate source of the government’s power. This exhibition is comprised of work reflecting artistic perceptions of the trajectory and success (or lack thereof) of this 250-year-old experiment. It depicts Americans going about their lives amidst the tensions between the foundational ideals of “We the People” and its imperfect realities. According to the exhibition’s curator, Jeremy Moss, “The world is in a state of fluctuation and full of challenges. ‘We the People’ documents how we see and face these challenges in the creative sphere…It is comprised of works of art that depict the emotions evoked by upheaval; clearly reflecting the diversity of ways in which artists reflect the immense challenges present in our society today.”

title: S.O.F.I.A. Welcomes the Community to its 16th Annual Walk Against Domestic Violence
location: Canterbury Park, Montclair, 07042, United States Minor Outlying Islands
description:
On Saturday, September 19, 2026, Start Out Fresh Intervention Advocates (S.O.F.I.A.) invites the community to affirm that “With Awareness There is Hope” at its 16th Annual Walk Against Domestic Violence in beautiful Canterbury Park. Registration for the Walk begins at 9 AM, the program begins at 10 AM, and the event ends at Noon. 
S.O.F.I.A. is thrilled to welcome Dr. Zakiyyah Green as Grand Marshal for our 16th Annual Walk Against Domestic Violence. Dr. Green is a longtime volunteer and advocate with S.O.F.I.A. As Executive director of W.I.S.E. and CEO of Ministry Without Walls, LLC, Dr. Green blends biblical wisdom with practical life strategies. A Certified Domestic Violence Advocate, Dr. Green’s message inspires healing, restoration, and resilience, encouraging all to overcome adversity and live transformed lives. 
Joining S.O.F.I.A.’s 16th Annual Walk Against Domestic Violence on September 19, 2026 means showing support through action and intent. S.O.F.I.A. holds its annual Walk Against Domestic Violence to show those affected by domestic violence, especially those still in abusive relationships, that they are not alone and that they have a network of support to hold them up. Joining us helps reduce the stigma and isolation of domestic violence. 
9:00 a.m. – 10:00 a.m.: Registration, snacks, and raffles
10:00 a.m. – 11:00 a.m.: Warm up and walk at your own pace!
11:15 a.m. – 11:45 a.m.: Grand Marshal – Dr. Zakiyyah Green and Recognitions
12:00 p.m. – Closing Meditation with the Community 
Registration for individuals starts at $20. Team Captains can pre-register for $45 and have team members sign up for $20 each. Teams can choose to represent a business, organization, or community group – a great way to highlight community involvement and values. We hope you’ll join us! See information here: http://supportsofia.org/events/ 
Thanks to a generous donation from EasyOptOuts.com, ALL who pre-register as a Team Captain and the first 20 individual registrants will receive a FREE year of membership to Easy Opt Outs, a privacy protection service. 
Those unable to join the event can walk virtually via social media posts and live broadcasts or make a donation directly to S.O.F.I.A. in honor or remembrance of a loved one via PayPal here: http://supportsofia.org/donate/, or send a check to S.O.F.I.A., PO Box 674, Montclair, NJ 07042.

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Saturdays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: Flow Into Form:  A Qi Gong and Expressive Art Experience
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Saturday September 19 | 1 – 3 pm, $40  
Breathe. Move. Create. 
Facilitated by Niraj Shah – long-time qi-gong teacher and practitioner, and Naz Botas – artist and owner of the Space. 
If you’ve been craving a gentle reset—something grounding, nourishing, and expressive—this workshop is your invitation. 
In this two-hour workshop, you’ll move through repeating cycles of Qi Gong and intuitive art-making designed to calm your nervous system, soften tension in the body, and open your creative heart. 
You’ll experience: 

Qi Gong: slow, mindful movements paired with gentle breathwork to flow your energy and bring you into the present moment
Intuitive Art: using charcoal, ink, or pastels, you’ll make marks on wall-length paper as your body moves — both naturally and through guided Qi Gong sequences — allowing your inner experience to express itself visually

Across the session, we’ll repeat several short rounds of movement followed by mark-making, gradually building comfort, curiosity, and expression. By the end, you’ll be able to look at your paper and literally see the journey your body and breath took you on. 
No prior experience in art or Qi Gong is needed. Just a willingness to breathe, move, and let the paper receive whatever wants to come through. 
Expect a peaceful, meditative atmosphere.
A safe space.
And a sense of release you’ll carry with you long after the workshop ends. 
These practices help you: 

Let go of stress stored in the body
Feel more present and grounded
Reconnect with your authentic creativity
Express yourself without pressure or judgment

A beautiful experience for anyone seeking clarity, calm, and creative freedom! 
What to Bring: 

comfortable clothing you can move in
a water bottle
an open heart and curious mind

title: Buena Vista Social Club: The musical
description:
Learn about the fascinating history of the Buena Vista Social Club—the band and the musical—in this lecture by Rick Feingold.

Program

Before the revolution altered the course of Cuban music, a band of young musicians in Havana in the 1950s had already begun to shake things up. In a surprising twist, the band reunited forty years later to record the songs they had left behind, and the result was the best-selling album in the history of world music. Years later, the band would become the subject of a Tony-winning Broadway musical. Feingold's presentation will focus on the musical and include clips from the 1999 documentary film Son Cubano, as well as a discussion of life in Cuba in the 1950s before the revolution.

Presenter

Rick Feingold oversaw the Latin Jazz series at the Performing Arts Center at Penn State University. In addition to extensive travels throughout Cuba, Feingold teaches history at Bergen Community College. Mr. Feingold has a Bachelor of Arts in History from Rutgers University and an MBA from Penn State University.

title: NJ Code & Coffee - September meetup
description:
NJ Code & Coffee
Calling all New Jersey techies to the monthly **NJ Code and Coffee** tech community meetup at the EqualSpace ES550 Tech & Innovation campus!

Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal networking/co-working session for those in tech (and the tech-curious).
That includes operators, founders, and investors. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, software engineers, solution architects... **all are welcome!**

People of all skill and experience levels can attend, we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, and many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. It's entirely up to you!

title: Valerie Huhn    A Life Rebuilt in Fingerprints
location: The BrassWorks Gallery, 105 Grove Street, Montclair, NJ, 07068, United States
description:
OPENING RECEPTION: Saturday, September 19, 4:00 – 6:00 PM
EXHIBITION RUNS: September 19 – December 18, 2026
Montclair, NJ — The BrassWorks Gallery is honored and delighted to present a solo exhibition of work by artist Valerie Huhn. The exhibition, A Life Rebuilt in Fingerprints, brings together two decades of Huhn’s signature fingerprint-based practice – sculptures, murals, and mixed-media works built from thousands of the artist’s own fingerprints – in a body of work that transforms a tool of surveillance and identification into a language of individuality, memory, and belonging.
For Huhn, this work is inseparable from her own history. As a teenager, she survived a car accident that left her with a traumatic brain injury – a neurological disability she still lives with today. In the aftermath, a series of misdiagnoses led to her placement in state and long-term psychiatric facilities, an experience that reshaped the course of her life. “I escaped from them to a world of art,” Huhn says. “I have hidden this injury from friends, relatives and coworkers. I understand its power to marginalize.”
That history is the root of the fingerprint work she has made for the past twenty years. Using her own right index finger, Huhn presses thousands of individually dated prints in a spectrum of colors onto sheets of clear acetate – deliberately avoiding black ink, the color of official booking records, in favor of a palette that reclaims the fingerprint as a mark of celebration rather than control. In much of the work, she hole-punches the colored prints into small disks and spears them in groups of four onto pins, a grouping inspired by the four nucleotides of DNA. She then uses these pins to cover books, furniture, clothing, and other everyday objects, building dense, glittering surfaces out of what is normally reduced to a tool of identification. The result is work that pushes back against the systems that once sorted her – and the communities she has lived among – into categories of control, replacing them with a record of individual, unrepeatable marks.
Valerie Huhn was honored with an Individual Artist Fellowship in Crafts from the New Jersey State Council on the Arts – one of the most competitive, sought-after distinctions available to a practicing New Jersey artist, awarded through an anonymous, peer-reviewed process. Huhn holds a BFA and MFA from the San Francisco Art Institute and studied at Parsons School of Design and the New School for Social Research. Her fingerprint-based work has been exhibited widely across the United States, including a 2007 exhibition in Washington, D.C. that launched her large-scale fingerprint murals, as well as solo and group shows at institutions including the Hunterdon Art Museum and the Morris Museum. She has completed residencies at chashama in New York and Aferro in Newark, and her work is held in public and private collections. .
For additional information contact Valerie Huhn; call or text 212-227-7522, email valerie.huhn@gmail.com, visit valeriehuhn.com,
or Instagram.com/valerie.huhn_.
The BrassWorks Gallery is open to the public Monday through Friday from 7:00 am to 7:00 pm. Housed in a beautifully restored 1930s industrial building that once served as the George Rutledge Etched Brass Works, the gallery honors Montclair’s rich history while supporting a vibrant contemporary art community.
BrassWorks is located at 105 Grove Street, Montclair, NJ. Originally constructed during the early twentieth century, 105 Grove Street was, for many years, home to the family-owned George Rutledge Etched Brass Works company. The property was converted into a unique professional office building in 2007 and provides space for a community art gallery. Upon learning the site’s heritage as home to a family-owned brass works company, the partners decided to transform the building while honoring its past by naming it BrassWorks on Grove. The present building combines modern amenities with the faithful restoration of the original 1930 architectural details.

title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776”
description:
The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. 
Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013.
Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ.
The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. 
With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. 
Those auditioning should prepare 16 to 32 bars of a song and bring sheet music for the accompanist. A bluetooth speaker will be available if needed. Actors will also be asked to read selections from the script. Please bring a résumé and photo. 
For information on cast and characters, please visit https://www.theaterleagueofclifton.com/ or email theaterleagueofclifton@gmail.com or call (973)-928-7668 
Founded in 2005, the Theater League of Clifton is a nonprofit community organization dedicated to fostering an appreciation of the arts through theatrical performances while providing quality entertainment for all ages. The Theater League of Clifton welcomes volunteers in all aspects of performance and production.

Music and Lyrics by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Book by PETER STONE
Based on a concept by SHERMAN EDWARDS

title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**

title: Schuylkill River Special Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this very interesting point to point hike in our Schuylkill River series! Distance will be about 15 miles and feature the Schuylkill River Trail, but also a lot of very interesting other things....
After meeting at the Schuylkill River Trail/Bartrum Trailhead on Market Street next to the Dry Wall place in Auburn PA, we will shuttle with as few vehicles as possible to the beginning.
The hike will begin covering the trail system at Kaercher Creek Park, which we've never visited before.
We'll weave around on most of their entire trail system, and then make our way through ball fields, and into downtown Hamburg.
We'll get on the Schuylkill River Trail here and mostly follow it back to Auburn area, but with some surprise side trips along the way.
One of the side trips will include locks and towpath on the Schuylkill Navigation that will be an out and back.
Most of the route will be pretty easy. The first bit will have a little bit of foot path, and one of the side trips may have some weeds, but nothing too terrible.
If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

Tantra Date for Couples: An Exploration Through the Senses
description:
Couples, 
Discover the art of conscious connection through awakening the senses. 
Most couples crave deeper touch, intimacy, and emotional connection. Yet, few of us were ever taught how to create experiences that genuinely feel extraordinary for both partners. 
Welcome to a brand-new, transformational date night designed to change that. These are guided experiential practices designed to help couples strengthen intimacy, communication, trust, and connection through simple but powerful embodied practices. 
Whether you are completely new to this work or have attended our events before, this experience is entirely new and different. It offers a safe, sacred, and nurturing space to step away from the noise of daily life and step into your bodies. Together, you will be guided on an immersive journey through the five senses—unlocking the unique wisdom, pleasure, and healing that each one has to offer. 
By the end of the event, you will have a deeper understanding of the transformative power of the senses and their role in accessing deeper states of pleasure and connection. You will leave feeling more grounded, present, connected to your body, connected to your partner, and with a renewed sense of vitality and passion for life and will know how to re-create these experiences at home. 
Tantra is a path of awakening and exploration that helps us move out of ordinary states into a sense of heightened awareness, expanded sensation. intimacy and mindfulness. 
What You Will Experience Together 

The Power of Touch: Learn how conscious, intentional touch becomes a direct gateway to deeper intimacy and sensual embodiment.
Sensory Awakening: Activate your senses through curated experiences with communication, mindfulness, smell, taste, and sound.
Elevated States: Discover how Tantra helps you move out of ordinary routines and into heightened awareness, expanded sensation, and profound bliss.
Safe Exploration: Participate in gentle, expertly guided practices designed to build deep mutual trust and comfort.

title: Walk at Grover Cleveland Park
description:
Let's Walk!!
**MEETING TIME 1:55 PM**

We will meet near the fishing pond entrance of the park, close to Brookside Avenue and the boat house/restrooms.
**GPS location: 138 Brookside Ave, Caldwell. Park on the street.**

We will walk for about 60-90 minutes at about a 3 miles/hour pace. The park has a paved path loop that is a little more than a mile. Stay for as many loops as you like.

We'll meet in front of the fishing pond at 1:55 and begin promptly at 2.

Grover Cleveland Park in Caldwell/Essex Fells celebrated its centennial in 2013. As the first county park in western Essex County, the site was originally selected for its natural beauty and its potential to provide a space for relaxation and recreation. It contains gentle rolling hills, broad meadows and other environmentally aesthetic features

**Please arrive 5 minutes early, so we can start on time.**

FOLLOW US ON INSTAGRAM - letswalkmeetup

Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.

title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776”
description:
The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. 
Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013.
Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ.
The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. 
With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. 
Those auditioning should prepare 16 to 32 bars of a song and bring sheet music for the accompanist. A bluetooth speaker will be available if needed. Actors will also be asked to read selections from the script. Please bring a résumé and photo. 
For information on cast and characters, please visit https://www.theaterleagueofclifton.com/ or email theaterleagueofclifton@gmail.com or call (973)-928-7668 
Founded in 2005, the Theater League of Clifton is a nonprofit community organization dedicated to fostering an appreciation of the arts through theatrical performances while providing quality entertainment for all ages. The Theater League of Clifton welcomes volunteers in all aspects of performance and production. 
1776
Music and Lyrics by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Book by PETER STONE
Based on a concept by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Original Production Directed by PETER HUNT
Originally Produced on the Broadway Stage by STUART OSTROW
1776 is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI.

title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776”
description:
The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. 
Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013.
Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ.
The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. 
With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. 
Those auditioning should prepare 16 to 32 bars of a song and bring sheet music for the accompanist. A bluetooth speaker will be available if needed. Actors will also be asked to read selections from the script. Please bring a résumé and photo. 
For information on cast and characters, please visit https://www.theaterleagueofclifton.com/ or email theaterleagueofclifton@gmail.com or call (973)-928-7668 
Founded in 2005, the Theater League of Clifton is a nonprofit community organization dedicated to fostering an appreciation of the arts through theatrical performances while providing quality entertainment for all ages. The Theater League of Clifton welcomes volunteers in all aspects of performance and production. 
1776
Music and Lyrics by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Book by PETER STONE
Based on a concept by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Original Production Directed by PETER HUNT
Originally Produced on the Broadway Stage by STUART OSTROW
1776 is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI.

description:

description:

Requirements:

Volunteers must be Food Safe Certified to participate.
Complete the certification by following the step-by-step instructions provided in this link.
Once certified, email your certification to foodrecoverynetwork@sgamsu.org to confirm your eligibility to participate.

Your involvement helps reduce food waste and insecurity while supporting individuals in our community who are in need. We look forward to your participation!*Please Note: This event end time is dependent on the amount of food given. You can estimate for max of hour and a half for recoveries.

title: Mental Health Support Group (NAMI's Connection Recovery Peer Support Group)
description:
The Essex-Passaic Chapter of NAMI (The National Alliance on Mental Illness) Connection Recovery Peer Support Group Program meets on the 4th Tuesday of each month at the West Caldwell Library on 30 Clinton Road. 

NAMI is the most influential organization devoted to helping people with mental illness and their relatives and loved ones recover and deal with mental health issues. These meetings will be led by people having some form of mental illness. During these meetings, we will conduct peer support though all people interested in this organization are encouraged to attend. You do not have to sign up in advance. All meetings are kept confidential and are led by people specifically trained to conduct these meetings.

 NAMI Connection is a recovery peer support group program that offers respect, understanding, encouragement and hope. NAMI Connection groups are:

·       Free and confidential

·       Held monthly for 90 minutes  

·       Designed to connect, encourage, and support participants using a structured support group model

·       Led by trained facilitators living in recovery themselves

This meeting is for anyone ages 18  who is dealing with their own mental illness or a loved one's.

title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776”
description:
The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. 
Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013.
Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ.
The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. 
With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. 
Those auditioning should prepare 16 to 32 bars of a song and bring sheet music for the accompanist. A bluetooth speaker will be available if needed. Actors will also be asked to read selections from the script. Please bring a résumé and photo. 
For information on cast and characters, please visit https://www.theaterleagueofclifton.com/ or email theaterleagueofclifton@gmail.com or call (973)-928-7668 
Founded in 2005, the Theater League of Clifton is a nonprofit community organization dedicated to fostering an appreciation of the arts through theatrical performances while providing quality entertainment for all ages. The Theater League of Clifton welcomes volunteers in all aspects of performance and production.

Music and Lyrics by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Book by PETER STONE
Based on a concept by SHERMAN EDWARDS

title: Tuesday Night Figure Drawing - Open Studio
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Tuesday Night Figure Drawing – Open Studio 
*Cover art by Ling Chen. 











Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and practice your drawing skills. 
Each week a different nude model serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say — observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. 
This has become a tight-knit, supportive community of seekers — artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion. Challenge your process if you have one, or begin to develop one if you don’t. Learn to truly see. 
Each session features a variety of poses, from quick gesture sketches to longer, more detailed studies. Whether you’re looking to sharpen your technical abilities, loosen up your line work, or simply enjoy the meditative experience of drawing from life, this open studio is designed to support individual growth in a collaborative atmosphere. All skill levels are welcome – we’ve even had poets drop in and compose verses to the vibe in the room. 
Bring your preferred supplies — charcoal, graphite, ink, pastels, and paint are all welcome. Basic drawing materials are available if you don’t have any, and the shop has drawing pads and supplies for sale. No formal instruction is provided, but peer feedback and self-guided exploration are always part of the mix. 
Good music. Good people. See you Tuesday. 7 – 9:30 pm at the Space. 
Tickets are set at a capacity of 12, but we accommodate up to 18 for those paying in cash. 











“The object isn’t to make art, its to be in that wonderful state which makes art inevitable.” – Robert Henri

title: FABRIC: Arts and Wellness series at Lackawanna Station
location: Lackawanna Plaza Montclair, NJ, Lackawanna Plaza, Montclair, NJ, 07042, United States
description:
FABRIC is a welcoming arts and wellness series designed for adults 55+ to foster creativity, connection, and well-being. Hosted by SAIVA at Lackawanna Station in Montclair, this program brings the community together through engaging, beginner-friendly experiences. By engaging this audience, the project preserves cultural heritage, strengthens social networks, and contributes to overall well-being, aligning directly with Essex County’s commitment to arts, culture, and community enrichment. 
Participants can enjoy: 
Gentle chair yoga and meditation sessions to support relaxation and mobility 
Creative art sessions that encourage self-expression 
A warm, social environment focused on building meaningful connections 
✨ Session Dates: 
Chair Yoga & Meditation at 11AM-12PM: May 20, July 22, September 23 
Art Sessions 2-3pm: June 17, August 19 
🎟️ Registration required | Limited to 20 participants per session 
No prior experience is needed. Each session is designed to be accessible, inclusive, and enriching. 
For Wellness Sessions: 
Take a deep breath… and give your body the gentle care it deserves. 
This welcoming chair yoga and meditation class is thoughtfully designed for seniors who want to feel stronger, more relaxed, and more at ease in their bodies—without getting down on the floor or pushing beyond their limits. Using a sturdy chair for support, you’ll move through simple, low-impact stretches and guided breathing that help improve flexibility, balance, and overall mobility in a safe and accessible way. 
Research shows that chair yoga can enhance strength, reduce joint pain and stiffness, and even improve balance and confidence with movement—helping to lower the risk of falls while supporting everyday activities. 
But this class is about more than movement… it’s about how you feel. 
Through gentle meditation and calming breathwork, you’ll learn simple tools to manage stress, quiet the mind, and reconnect with a sense of inner calm. These practices activate the body’s natural relaxation response, helping to reduce anxiety, improve mood, and support better sleep. 
You’ll leave each session feeling: 
• More grounded and centered 
• Gently stretched and energized 
• Mentally clear and relaxed 
No experience is needed—just come as you are. Every movement can be modified, and you are always encouraged to go at your own pace. 
This is a supportive, feel-good environment where you can move, breathe, and connect—not just with your body, but with a sense of calm, stability, and well-being that carries into your everyday life. 
Because it’s never too late to feel better in your body… and more at peace in your mind.

title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes)
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: Wine Confidence 101
location: Montclair - Cornerstone Montclair, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Build your wine confidence in just four weeks. Whether you are new to wine or already a
connoisseur, this approachable course will give you the knowledge, tasting skills, and
vocabulary to enjoy wine more fully—and choose it more confidently.

Throughout this 4-week course, you will explore the world’s primary grape varieties and
discover the many styles of white, rosé, red, and sparkling wines. We will break down
the basics of viticulture and winemaking so you can understand how grapes, regions,
and production choices shape the flavors, aromas, body, and texture in every glass. You
will also learn what makes the major wine-producing countries distinctive and how to
recognize key differences among grape varieties and wine styles.

Each session includes guided tasting practice, from visual assessment through aroma,
flavor, structure, and finish, helping you evaluate wine and learn why you like or dislike
different wines. Durin the 4 weeks, we will taste 20–25 wines from around the world,
making this class both educational and delicious. By the end, you will feel more
comfortable ordering, buying, discussing, and enjoying wine in any setting.

THIS EVENT IS 21  Students will be required to show a government ID to the instructor
upon arriving at the first session.

title: Weekly Food Recovery Initiative
description:
Join our weekly Food Recovery events, where dedicated volunteers and members gather to make a difference in our community. Each week, participants help collect perfectly good leftover food from Gourmet Dining and transport it to Blanton. There, the food is repackaged into individual microwavable containers and stocked in the food pantry, providing meals for those in need throughout the week. 
To Participate: RSVP to attend the event each week. Meet in Blanton Hall Residence Hall Kitchenette in the Communal Area (Tell them you are working with Food Recovery), Sign in via Event Pass and your set!
Requirements:

Volunteers must be Food Safe Certified to participate.
Complete the certification by following the step-by-step instructions provided in this link.
Once certified, email your certification to foodrecoverynetwork@sgamsu.org to confirm your eligibility to participate.

Your involvement helps reduce food waste and insecurity while supporting individuals in our community who are in need. We look forward to your participation!*Please Note: This event end time is dependent on the amount of food given. You can estimate for max of hour and a half for recoveries.

title: 'The Shoes' Play Reading
description:
Come enjoy a reading of The Shoes before it hits the New York Theatre Festival (NYWinterfest) this winter!


The Shoes follows the story of Kent Warner, the man who changed the course of Hollywood history when he discovered Judy Garland's iconic ruby slippers from The Wizard of Oz hidden away in storage. Yet, behind the glitz and glamour of showbiz, Kent struggled with his identity, a sense of belonging, and the search for love—often using his passion for classic cinema to escape his own reality.

In a world of good and bad witches, of empty heads and aching hearts, Kent ultimately proved to be the courage at the center of it all.

A former New York Times reporter, she is the co-author of two nonfiction books, and she and her husband have two children and live in Maplewood, NJ. She’s on Facebook, BlueSky, x.com, and Instagram.

title: Library Speakers Consortium - Where the Paletero Man Goes: A Journey of Neighborhood, Music, and Art with Lucky Diaz (English)
description:
You must register here to attend: https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/197986

Grab a pocketful of change and get ready to dance down the street! Join us for an energetic conversation as we celebrate the joy of community and summer fun with Latin GRAMMY-winning musician Lucky Diaz, author of the sensational bilingual picture book, Paletero Man. 

What’s the best way to cool off on a hot summer day? Run quick and find Paletero José!

Follow along with our narrator as he passes through his busy neighborhood in search of the Paletero Man. But when he finally catches up with him, our narrator’s pockets are empty. Oh no! What happened to his dinero? It will take the help of the entire community to get the tasty treat now.

Inspired by the vibrant rhythms of Los Angeles and Diaz’s own hit song, this beautiful story invites readers into a sun-drenched neighborhood where the ring of a bell means the best treat of the day is just around the corner.

Register today and discover how we can all bring a little more sweetness and community spirit into our daily lives!

Please note that we will be hosting Lucky Diaz twice on this date, once in Spanish and in English. Be sure that you are registering for your preferred format.

About the Author:

Lucky Diaz is a GRAMMY Award-winning, multi–Latin GRAMMY Award-winning artist, acclaimed author, and a leading voice in contemporary children’s literature. A six-time Emmy-nominated songwriter and Berklee College of Music alumnus, Diaz made history as the first North American children’s artist to win a Latin GRAMMY. His work bridges music and storytelling, creating a distinct body of bilingual work rooted in the cultural life of Mexican American communities in Los Angeles.

As an author, Diaz has earned some of the highest honors in publishing. His books have received starred reviews from Kirkus Reviews, School Library Journal, Publishers Weekly, and Booklist, placing him among a rare group of creators recognized across every major literary journal. His breakout title Paletero Man received a Kirkus star and audiobook distinction and was awarded the 2024 Alma Flor Ada Award for its lasting contribution to Latino-centered storytelling. He is also a recipient of the Parent’s Choice Gold Award and a NAPPA Award, further recognizing his impact on family audiences.

His latest book, Fix-It Familia, continues to build national recognition, with a Spanish edition arriving this summer, expanding access to bilingual readers and classrooms across the country.

Diaz’s work has been featured and praised by NPR, Billboard, The New York Times, and People Magazine, positioning him as a trusted creative voice at the intersection of culture, music, and literature.

Through his books, recordings, and performances with Lucky Diaz and the Family Jam Band, Diaz continues to expand the possibilities of American storytelling. He is not only contributing to the field. He is helping define it.

title: Library Speakers Consortium - Paletero Man: un viaje por el barrio, la música y el arte con Lucky Diaz (Español)
description:
Debes registrarte aquí para asistir: https://libraryc.org/nutleypubliclibrary/198667

La duración de este evento será de 30 minutos.

Agarra un puñado de monedas y prepárate para bailar por la calle. Únete a nosotros para una enérgica conversación mientras celebramos la alegría de la comunidad y la diversión del verano con Lucky Diaz, músico ganador del premio Latin GRAMMY y autor del sensacional libro ilustrado bilingüe, Paletero Man.

¿Cuál es la mejor manera de refrescarse en un caluroso día de verano? ¡Corre rápido y encuentra al Paletero José!

Sigue a nuestro narrador mientras recorre su ajetreado vecindario en busca del Paletero Man. Pero cuando finalmente lo alcanza, los bolsillos de nuestro narrador están vacíos. ¡Oh no! ¿Qué pasó con su dinero? Se necesitará la ayuda de toda la comunidad para conseguir la sabrosa golosina ahora.

Inspirada en los vibrantes ritmos de Los Ángeles y la exitosa canción de Diaz, esta hermosa historia invita a los lectores a un vecindario bañado por el sol donde el sonido de una campana significa que la mejor golosina del día está a la vuelta de la esquina.

¡Regístrate hoy y descubre cómo todos podemos aportar un poco más de dulzura y espíritu comunitario a nuestra vida diaria!

Ten en cuenta que presentaremos a Lucky Diaz dos veces en esta fecha, una en español y otra en inglés. Asegúrate de registrarte para el formato que prefieras.

Acerca del autor:

Lucky Diaz es un artista ganador del premio GRAMMY, multi-ganador del premio Latin GRAMMY, aclamado autor y una voz líder en la literatura infantil contemporánea. Compositor nominado seis veces al premio Emmy y ex alumno de Berklee College of Music, Diaz hizo historia como el primer artista infantil norteamericano en ganar un Latin GRAMMY. Su trabajo une música y narración, creando un cuerpo distintivo de trabajo bilingüe arraigado en la vida cultural de las comunidades mexicano-americanas en Los Ángeles.

Como autor, Diaz ha obtenido algunos de los más altos honores en el mundo editorial. Sus libros han recibido reseñas destacadas de Kirkus Reviews, School Library Journal, Publishers Weekly y Booklist, lo que lo sitúa entre un raro grupo de creadores reconocidos en todas las principales publicaciones literarias. Su título revelación Paletero Man recibió una estrella de Kirkus y una distinción de audiolibro y fue galardonado con el Premio Alma Flor Ada 2024 por su contribución duradera a la narración centrada en los latinos. También ha recibido el Parent’s Choice Gold Award y un NAPPA Award, lo que reconoce aún más su impacto en el público familiar.

Su último libro, Fix-It Familia, sigue generando reconocimiento nacional, con una edición en español que llegará este verano, ampliando el acceso a lectores bilingües y aulas en todo el país.

El trabajo de Diaz ha sido presentado y elogiado por NPR, Billboard, The New York Times y People Magazine, lo que lo posiciona como una voz creativa confiable en la intersección de la cultura, la música y la literatura.

A través de sus libros, grabaciones y presentaciones con Lucky Diaz and the Family Jam Band, Diaz continúa ampliando las posibilidades de la narración estadounidense. No solo está contribuyendo al campo. Está ayudando a definirlo.

title: CEDAR GROVE PARK WALK
description:
Let's Walk!!
You can **park** in the **Robert J. O'Toole Community Center** parking lot located at **199 Fairview Ave, Cedar Grove, NJ 07009**

**Meet us under the gazebos** at the park directly across the street.

We will be walking the paved walking path that meanders over foot bridges and past little “workout stations.”

We will walk about 3 - 4 miles. There are options to break off from the walk if you need to.

Bathrooms are available.

Cedar Grove Park is the newest addition to the Essex County Park System, formally dedicated on December 12, 2016. At 77 acres, it is the fourth largest park in the county parks system. The park features the Robert J. O'Toole Community Center, four bocce courts, a farm themed playground area and three fitness stations along meandering walking paths.

Rain or extreme weather will cancel the event.

PLEASE ARRIVE 5 MINUTES PRIOR TO START TIME.

If you have any questions, call the leader. **Temperatures above 90 degrees and steady rain cancels, but intermittent drizzle does not. You will *not* be notified.** **Bring water. Wear hiking boots, preferably waterproof with good soles and traction devices and bring poles (optional).** Dogs are not allowed on hikes unless specified.
These hikes are publicized first to SMC members and then advertised to the public one week before a hike. There is a limit of 25 participants, so pre-registration is required at least two days before a hike to sign the liability waiver online and allow lists to be sent to hike leaders. If you have registered and then find you cannot attend, please cancel your order online. **Repeated no shows without prior cancellation will result in removal from list.**
**To become a current member visit [[https://www.somocon.org/membership/](https://www.somocon.org/membership/)]([https://www.somocon.org/membership/](https://www.somocon.org/membership/)).**

description:
A book club for adults who want to read in community. We meet one Friday morning a month to chat about a title we read in common.

--
Back to School September: Reading the Classics

SULA 
by Toni Morrison (1973)

A modern masterpiece about love and kinship, about living in an America birthed from slavery. Nobel Prize laureate Toni Morrison gives life to characters who struggle with what society tells them to be, and the love they long for and crave as Black women. (from the publisher)

--

Reading club participants are also encouraged to read the chapter on Sula (pp 49-70) in:

ON MORRISON
by Namwali Serpell (2026)
**pages 49-70 only

Toni Morrison, Nobel Laureate and one of our most beloved writers, has inspired generations of readers. But her artistic genius is often overshadowed by her monumental public persona, perhaps because, as Namwali Serpell puts it, “she is our only truly canonical black female writer—and her work is highly complex.” In On Morrison, Serpell brings her unique experience as both an award-winning writer and a professor who teaches a course on Morrison to illuminate her masterful experiments with literary form. This is Morrison as you’ve never encountered her before, a journey through her oeuvre...with contextual guidance and original close readings. At once accessible and uncompromisingly rigorous, On Morrison is a primer not only on how to read one of the most significant American authors of all time but also on how to read great works of literature in general. This dialogue on the page between two black women artist-readers is stylish, edifying, and thrilling in its scope and intelligence. (from the publisher)

Copies of both books will be available at the Circulation Desk starting September 1.

title: The Space for Words - Literary Open-mic
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
The Space for Words – Literary Open-mic night hosted by the NJ Poetry Circle
September 25  |  Doors open at 7:30, start time 8 pm  |  $10 for everyone 
This is a monthly event on the last Friday of every month, holidays permitting. 
Hey writers, poets, and storytellers!  Come share your art with us at The Space for Words Open Mic Night. Whether you’re a seasoned author or just getting started, this is your chance to share your work in front of a supportive and inspiring audience. 
Bring your poetry, short stories, or excerpts from your latest work — the stage is yours! The Space is a safe place to try out new material, read old favorites, experiment with a different genre, and even to sing a song if inspiration strikes you. Each performer gets a maximum of 5 minutes to read, and at the end we take time to socialize and vibe with one another. 
Come for the words, stay for the community. The Space for Words has grown into an amazing community of writers supporting one another. This event is open to all levels and all genres, so whether you write fiction, non-fiction, memoir, or poetry, we want to hear from you. It’s all about celebrating the power of storytelling in a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere. All of our open mic nights are always inclusive. 
Anyone who puts their name in the bucket upon entry gets a shot at the mic, and has a maximum of 5 minutes. Depending on how many people sign up and if time allows, we can have people come up a second time. 
Audience members are, as always, a welcome and vital part of these performances. 
If you have published books that you would like to sell, bring some copies and be prepared to accept payment. 
General guidelines: 

Hate speech of any kind is never allowed and will be shut down.
Violence or references to physical harm to others will be shut down.

BYOB is welcome, and some light snacks and drinks are served. 
Accessibility: The Space is located on the second floor of a historic building, accessible via a flight of stairs. Unfortunately, there is no elevator access at this time. This means we are unable to accommodate wheelchairs or guests with significant mobility challenges. We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this may cause.

title: [Outside Org]  Aging in Montclair Saturday Social
Afternoon Tea & Dessert Pairing
description:
We invite you to join us for a special Chinese tea and traditional music event. In this one-hour presentation, we will learn about Chinese gongfu tea, its cultural significance and mythical origins, taste three single-origin teas (green, white, and oolong), and conclude with a guzheng performance. 

Chinese gongfu tea is a method of brewing tea with time and effort, allowing us to control the time, temperature, and quantity of the brew to maximize the tea’s flavor. It encourages us to slow down a moment in our day, to focus on what’s in the cup, and appreciate what nature can create. Registration is required. 


Marjorie Wang grew up in NJ, and attended university in Shanghai, where she fell in love with Chinese teas. After an apprenticeship at NYC's Tea Drunk, she began sharing her passion with local communities through tea tasting events at libraries, community centers, and clubs. She has been playing the guzheng since age 12, and continues to perform at local cultural events.

title: Sonic Sound Healing Experience with @RightontimeTay
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Sonic Sound Healing Experience with @RightontimeTay
Saturday, September 26 · 7:00 – 8:30 PM 
Join us for a sonic healing journey with local DJ @RightontimeTay, who blends crystal bowls with intentionally chosen tracks to restore the body to resonance. Picture the lights dimmed low, the room falling away, and nothing left but sound – waves of tone rippling across your skin, low frequencies humming in your chest, crystal bowls ringing out long after they’ve been struck. Taylor curates sound journeys of all kinds, and this one is designed to let you fully rest: a ride through nostalgia, exploration, and fantasia, carried by tone and texture rather than words. 
We’re timing this with the full moon, harnessing that energy as part of the experience. In sound healing traditions, the full moon marks the peak of the lunar cycle – the moment everything you’ve been carrying rises to the surface and is ready to be released. It’s a night for letting go of what’s grown stagnant, for clarity to surface, for whatever you’ve been holding onto to finally move. The bowls and tones do the work of loosening it; the moon does the work of amplifying it. 
You’ll spend the evening lying on the floor, eyes closed, letting the sound wash over and through you – no tension, no talking, just full-body immersion in the wave, released a little further with every tone. 
Come with an open mind. Bring a yoga mat (or something soft to lie on) and a water bottle to stay hydrated – sound baths can pull you deep, and you’ll want to come back out nourished. Beyond that, you have nowhere else to be but to be! 
Please give yourself enough time to park and arrive before 7pm. 
After the sound journey, stay for The Unwind, community dance party! 
Taylor will keep the vibes coming for us after the sound journey with gentle tunes that will get our bodies moving.  Your ticket for the sound healing gets you into the dance party, but you can also invite friends and family to join you for the dance portion.  $10 tickets are sold separately for those not attending the sound healing, and can be purchased here.

title: The Unwind - Post Sound Healing Dance Party with @RightontimeTay
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Saturday, September 26 · 9:00 PM · $10 
Following the Sonic Sound Healing that starts at 7pm.  Tickets for that are sold here. 
After the sound bath winds down, the night doesn’t have to end — it just changes shape. Come dance it out at The Unwind, a low-pressure, all-are-welcome dance session for anyone who wants to keep moving after the bowls go quiet. 
This isn’t a club night. There’s no social pressure, set choreography, or a “right” way to move. Think soft lighting, a thoughtfully built playlist, and a room full of people swaying, stepping, and shaking loose whatever the sound healing stirred up. Come as you are — sweatpants, bare feet, eyes closed if you want them closed. Dance alone, dance with a stranger, or just sway in place. All bodies, all skill levels, all moods welcome. 
It’s the perfect way to integrate a sound healing session, moving what’s been released, letting it settle into the body through motion instead of stillness. And if you’re just joining us for The Unwind on its own, that’s welcome too. 
Bring water, bring comfortable shoes (or none at all), and bring whatever energy you’ve got. We’ll do the rest.

title: Boonton Area Loop Hike and Railroad History Visit
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this loop hike around Boonton NJ area, which will feature parks we have done as well as not done, connected by short back street jaunts.
The main theme is that we will walk to and through the Tri State Railway Historical Society Open House day, featuring a huge collection of vintage rail stuff!
After we meet at the Acme, we'll walk back streets and fields to the event to arrive shortly after it starts.
Then after we spend an hour or so there, we'll continue on some different community trails. We will weave through and cover as much of this as possible that we have not done before, as well as ones we have such as the Trolley Trail and the Tourne.
How much of the stuff we do will depending on how we are doing on mileage and how much daylight we have.
We may adjust our route along the way. Planned route is about 15 miles.
Cost for entry is $10 at the door for adults or $8 online preordered.
If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Sundays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.
source: Meetup: NJ Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More

title: * POSTPONED - Reimagining the Tarot:  An Intuitive Collage Workshop
description:
This month’s edition is postponed to a future date, to be announced.  Please join our Tea & Tarot events in the meantime! 
What if the Tarot could speak in your voice? 
In this exploratory workshop, we’ll dive into the rich history and symbolism of the Major Arcana — exploring the colors, archetypes, and allegories that have given these iconic cards their power for centuries. Then, we’ll turn that wisdom over to your own creative instincts. 
No art experience needed. No tarot experience needed. Just an open mind and a willingness to listen to what’s stirring inside you. 
You’ll choose a card that calls to you, journal your reflections, and then bring it to life through drawing, painting, or collage — reimagining it through your own symbols, style, and personal expression. The goal isn’t perfection; it’s presence. We’re letting intuition lead. 
📅 Sunday, September 27 | 12:30 pm – 3:00 pm 📍 The Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Loft #2, Montclair, NJ 🎟 
 The first 1.5 hours is the lecture about the major arcana and symbolism for $45  
Returning participants can choose to skip the lecture and arrive at 2:00 pm for $20 for the collage portion 
What You’ll Do: 

Explore the Major Arcana and the art of symbolic storytelling
Choose a card that resonates with you in the moment
Journal your insights and reflections
Sketch and plan your own symbolic design
Create your unique version of the card through your medium of choice.  Collage materials, magazines, paint, colored pencils and markers will be available.

All materials provided. Just bring your imagination, an open mind, a tarot deck, and a notebook. 
This is an on-going series that allows you to build on your personal deck through repeated attendance. 
  
Your Guide Gina Devine
Instagram: @gina.devine 

Gina Devine is an esoteric artist, intuitive tarot reader, writer, educator and guide. 
She has provided thousands of readings for people all over the world, and leads both protection and tarot workshops. Her approach to guidance is loving, grounded and human. Although she also teaches traditional tarot classes, her tea and tarot discussion group was birthed from the knowing that people are more inclined to to be in tune with the archetypes of the cards and the messages they bring when they are allowed space to enjoy the tarot in a more casual setting – instead of forcefully trying to memorize them. The same way we find joy in discussing a book in community, the cards also call for us to convene together around them. Her approach is philosophical, therapeutic and creative, and she is on a mission to guide people toward unearthing a more intimate and honest relationship with their inner knowing through the art of divination. You can find her services and more at soulcentrictarot.com 

👉 Sign up for the Soul Centric Tarot Newsletter

title: Dismantling Anti-Semitism (B'nai Keshet)
location: Temple B’nai Keshet, 99 S Fullerton Ave, Montclair, NJ, 07042, United States
description:
This session will include individual and congregational storytelling by allied communities related to race, antisemitism, and white nationalism; grounding in skills like deep listening and constructive feedback; interactive analysis of the intertwined histories of racism and antisemitism; and contemporary challenges to interfaith solidarity movements. 
To Register Click HERE  
Questions? Please reach out to Bnai Keshet member Jessica Brater or Rev. Katrina 
About the Facilitator 
Megan Black Johnson is a trainer, facilitator, and organizer who has spent much of her career trying to make sense of our differences and build bridges between them. Trained in community organizing and interfaith solidarity, since 2010 Megan has worked with organizations like Interfaith America, Faith in Action, JOIN for Justice, and Western States Center to navigate the divisions created by race, religion, and politics, with a particular focus on the issues of antisemitism, anti-Black racism, and Christian hegemony. Megan earned her undergraduate degree from the University of Notre Dame and a Master of Divinity degree from Vanderbilt University. She now directs a program to counter antisemitism and protect democracy at Western States Center and regularly trains and facilitates bridge-building initiatives across the country. Megan and her husband (an ordained priest in the Episcopal church) are travel enthusiasts, casual cyclists, active in their Episcopal church community, and proud, exhausted parents of a toddler. They live in Baltimore, Maryland.

title: Long Pose Figure Drawing and Painting
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Long Pose Figure Drawing and Painting 
Cover art by Jake Yeh 
Sunday, September 27, 1 – 5 pm, $10 per hour or $35 for the full session 
“The object isn’t to make art, it’s to be in that wonderful state which makes art inevitable.” – Robert Henri 
This special Sunday session is an extended version of our beloved Tuesday night figure drawing, giving you a full four hours to sink deep into the work. Bring your favorite materials, settle in, listen to some good tunes in great company, and get into your flow.  This will be a great opportunity to create a more finished work of art, hone your portraiture skills, or work with a material that you don’t normally get to use. 
Our model will be dressed in character (more details coming soon) and serve as our muse for the afternoon.  Whether you want to loosen up your line work, push into a sustained study, or simply spend a slow Sunday afternoon drawing from life, this is your space to do it. 
You can stay for the full session, or drop in and pay by the hour for an hour or two. 
All skill levels welcome, from seasoned studio artists to total beginners. Even poets have been known to drop in. 
Materials such as charcoal, graphite, ink, pastels, and paints are all welcome. Basic drawing supplies available upon request. No formal instruction is given so it is a self-guided session. 
Check out our regular weekly Tuesday night sessions here.

title: Lenore Raphael Trio performs Jazz standards
description:
Program

The Lenore Raphael Trio consists of Lenore on piano, Hilliard Greene on bass, and Kahlil Kwame Bell on drums, creating a world-class ensemble. Their performance will feature jazz classics and selections from the American songbook.

 

Artist

Lenore Raphael is a jazz pianist, radio personality, Steinway artist, and jazz educator who is widely considered to be among the top pianists working in modern music. Major jazz clubs and festivals have sold out her performances on multiple occasions. New York City's Birdland, The Blue Note, and Jazz at Lincoln Center were all stops for Dizzy's, and among them are the following: the Ottawa International Jazz Festival, Ronnie Scott's in London, the S.S. Oosterdam jazz cruise, the Tel Aviv Jazz Festival, and multiple others. The Joy Of Jazz event in Johannesburg, South Africa, featured three internationally known Steinway pianists, including Abdullah Ibraham and Ahmad Jamal. She was one of them. Additionally, in April 2014, Lenore played to sold-out crowds at the Broward Center for the Arts Amaturo theater in Ft. Lauderdale, Florida, and the Casa Da Musica in Porto, Portugal. England, Europe, and Israel have all been stops on her tour. She had a giant tour in South Africa in 2016, and every place she played there requested her to come back.

title: Celebrate the publication Shibu's New Friend with author Tess Thomas (recommended for ages 4-8)
location: Montclair Main - Green Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
Join author Tess Thomas for a special storytime at the Montclair Public Library! Tess will read her debut picture book, SHIBU'S TAIL, as well as her brand-new sequel, SHIBU'S NEW FRIEND. The books follow the adventures of a cat named Shibu, who has big feelings and an even bigger tail. SHIBU'S TAIL has earned four starred reviews, multiple best-of-year lists, and has been published in over 18 different countries. Following the readings, Tess will answer questions from the audience and lead young readers in a Shibu and Dottie-themed craft. Copies of SHIBU'S TAIL and SHIBU'S NEW FRIEND will be available for purchase and signing following the event.

Registration is recommended but not required.

 



Tess Thomas is a writer living in Hoboken, New Jersey. She started her storytelling career at the age of four, when she would dictate tales about her imaginary friends, Sami the cat and Doodie the dog, and send them to her grandparents. Her first book, SHIBU'S TAIL, earned four starred reviews, multiple best-of-year lists, and has been published in over a dozen different languages. Tess’ favorite part of being an author is visiting schools, libraries, and bookstores to connect with young readers. She loves french fries, her kids, and her husband (sometimes in that order).

SHIBU'S NEW FRIEND

Shibu and Dottie are as different as cats and dogs — but maybe they have more in common than they think in this charming sequel to the international hit SHIBU'S TAIL!

Shibu has a lot of friends and they have a lot in common. It’s a lot of fun! But then comes … Dottie. Dottie is a DOG and she does things a bit differently. She barks instead of purrs. She tears up boxes instead of sitting inside them. She spends a lot of time … digging?

Shibu isn’t sure about a new friend, especially one so different, but he can’t help feeling like Dottie’s love for life is a lot like his own. Could this new friend actually become his best pal? Published by Levine Querido, SHIBU'S NEW FRIEND hits shelves on September 1, 2026!

description:

To Participate: RSVP to attend the event each week. Meet in Blanton Hall Residence Hall Kitchenette in the Communal Area (Tell them you are working with Food Recovery), Sign in via Event Pass and your set!
Requirements:

Volunteers must be Food Safe Certified to participate.
Complete the certification by following the step-by-step instructions provided in this link.
Once certified, email your certification to foodrecoverynetwork@sgamsu.org to confirm your eligibility to participate.

Your involvement helps reduce food waste and insecurity while supporting individuals in our community who are in need. We look forward to your participation!*Please Note: This event end time is dependent on the amount of food given. You can estimate for max of hour and a half for recoveries.

title: Movie Screening of Politics is a Mother: Raising Hell is Part of the Job
location: College of Coms and Media: Presentation Hall
description:
At 79 years old, New Jersey Senator Loretta Weinberg wasn’t slowing down—she was at the height of her influence and just getting started.
Affectionately known as the “Feisty Grandma,” the former Senate majority leader built a reputation for challenging powerful figures, standing up for what she believed in, and refusing to stay quiet. She turned New Jersey politics upside down when she helped uncover the infamous Bridgegate scandal, contributing to Governor Chris Christie’s dramatic fall from power and proving that determination can shake even the strongest political establishment.
But behind the headlines, heated debates, and political victories is a warm and wonderfully complicated mother-daughter story. Told through that personal lens, Politics Is a Mother: Raising Hell Is Part of the Job offers a funny, heartfelt, and revealing look at the woman behind the public figure. It explores how family shaped Weinberg’s political life—and how politics became part of the family.
Full of humor, heart, history, and a healthy dose of hell-raising, this story shows why the political is always personal. It also proves that an “adorable grandmother” can be a fearless advocate, a relentless reformer, and one of the most important and influential politicians of our time.

Hosted by: Civic & Voter Engagement, Government Relations and Community Affairs

title: The Library of Alexandria NEW
location: Montclair Main - Auditorium, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

The Library of Alexandria was the ancient world's boldest experiment: an attempt to gather every book on earth under one roof. Its story has become intertwined with famous figures like Cleopatra and Julius Caesar, making it difficult to separate fact from legend. Did it hold half a million scrolls? Did it burn to the ground in a single night? This talk explores who filled its shelves, who studied there, and what really happened to it. We'll then visit the Bibliotheca Alexandrina, the impressive modern library that opened in 2002 near where the ancient one once stood.

Presented by Jenny Montasir, Montclair State professor and founder of EgyptEd.

title: The Assembly of Lovers - Sufi Drum Circle
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Community drum and chant circle rooted in Sufi prayer. 
Meets every other Monday:  September 28, October 12, etc. 
Contribution: Sliding scale donation $20–$40 (no one will be turned away) 
This is a vibrant Community Drum and Chanting Circle, where we drum and chant from our hearts into the universe. This experience is open to absolutely everyone, regardless of background or belief system—all that’s required is an open heart and a willingness to connect through sound.  The term ‘lover’ in this context refers to seekers on the Sufi path who are longing for union with the divine energy.  You can think of this gathering as an expansion of the sema sufi meditations we used to offer.  It is looser in form, more focused on music, and does not necessarily involve whirling, although it is welcome if you are called to it. 
There is a rhythm older than thought. A pulse that moves beneath language, beneath belief, beneath the self that thinks it’s separate. The Mystics knew this. The Sufis practiced it in Majalis al-‘Ushshāq. The Assembly of Lovers. Not lovers of ideas. Not lovers of comfort. Lovers magnetized by the Beloved. Those who’ve tasted the Divine Honey and cannot forget. Whose hearts remember what the mind has been taught to ignore. This is a gathering for those who feel the pull. The Assembly of Lovers meets twice each month, a rhythm of remembrance. Each gathering deepens the last. The circle becomes a living pulse of devotion. If you have a drum, bring it. Medicine drums, frame drums, and ceremony drums are all welcome. The circle grows stronger when every heartbeat joins the rhythm. 
The Flow 
Opening (5 minutes)
We set intention. A short prayer to open the way. To align the heart toward what is Real. 
Chanting and Rhythm (30-40 minutes)
Using the Sufi Chants of the Heart as a guide (our vision is for the chants to grow to what the individuals in the circle are inspired to invoke), we share simple chants. The drum holds the pulse. The voice follows. The meanings are offered, not explained. 
Repetition is the technology. The heart softens through return. Through invoking the Divine until the one invoking dissolves. 
Silent Resting (5-10 minutes)
After the chanting, we sit. No guidance. No instruction. 
The echo of the words and rhythms settles. The heart rests in what was touched. 
Closing (5 minutes)
A prayer of Unity. Of Oneness. We complete the circle and return to silence. 
Gratitude for what was offered. For what was received. 
  
Who This Is For 
This is for those who’ve felt the pull and don’t know what to call it. 
For those tired of spiritual talk that never touches the ground. 
For those who suspect that the heart knows a language the mind cannot translate. 
For those who long. 
Not for something. Not for someone. 
Just longing itself. The flame that keeps you moving toward what you cannot name but cannot forget. 
Osama Janakat 
 
Osama studied Mathematics and Physics at Rutgers University, laying a foundation of analytical thinking that complements his creative pursuits. As a beat-maker and music producer, he explores the intriguing connections between music, philosophy, and spirituality. 
Born in Jordan with Circassian roots, Osama’s move to the US in 2004 sparked a journey of inner exploration and spiritual discovery. An avid student of the Sufi tradition, he continues to seek wisdom that bridges cultures and disciplines, finding harmony in the interplay of art and spirituality.

title: Tuesday Night Figure Drawing - Open Studio
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Tuesday Night Figure Drawing – Open Studio 
*Cover art by Ling Chen. 











Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and practice your drawing skills. 
Each week a different nude model serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say — observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. 
This has become a tight-knit, supportive community of seekers — artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion. Challenge your process if you have one, or begin to develop one if you don’t. Learn to truly see. 
Each session features a variety of poses, from quick gesture sketches to longer, more detailed studies. Whether you’re looking to sharpen your technical abilities, loosen up your line work, or simply enjoy the meditative experience of drawing from life, this open studio is designed to support individual growth in a collaborative atmosphere. All skill levels are welcome – we’ve even had poets drop in and compose verses to the vibe in the room. 
Bring your preferred supplies — charcoal, graphite, ink, pastels, and paint are all welcome. Basic drawing materials are available if you don’t have any, and the shop has drawing pads and supplies for sale. No formal instruction is provided, but peer feedback and self-guided exploration are always part of the mix. 
Good music. Good people. See you Tuesday. 7 – 9:30 pm at the Space. 
Tickets are set at a capacity of 12, but we accommodate up to 18 for those paying in cash. 











“The object isn’t to make art, its to be in that wonderful state which makes art inevitable.” – Robert Henri

title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes)
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

September's movie matinees are for those excited for the first day of Autumn (Sept. 22), light cardigans and crisp mornings. Get cozy and join us at the library for some Fall favorites!


Remember The Titans (2000) | PG

In Virginia, high school football is a way of life, an institution revered, each game celebrated more lavishly than Christmas, each playoff distinguished more grandly than any national holiday. And with such recognition, comes powerful emotions. In 1971 high school football was everything to the people of Alexandria. But when the local school board was forced to integrate an all black school with an all white school, the very foundation of football's great tradition was put to the test. Watch the trailer here.

Seating is first come, first served. Registration is not required, but recommended for reminders and updates.

title: Nutrition Trends + Myths
description:
Have you ever seen a TikTok about a new diet, food, or recipe that someone claimed "fixed all their problems?" You're not the only one! Non-nutrition professionals in media love to talk about nutrition like they're experts, but do you know how to identify the professionals from the influencers? Come to this MSDO meeting to explore current nutrition trends circulating the media, learn how to critically analyze information you view, and maybe even engage in some interesting conversations about your own nutrition beliefs. This space is welcome to all, and this includes different belief systems around food. This will not be a space to shame, guilt, or tell you if what you're eating is right or wrong. We encourage everyone to come with an open-mind and the curiosity to know more!
