title: Wine Confidence 101
location: Montclair - Cornerstone Montclair, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Build your wine confidence in just four weeks. Whether you are new to wine or already a
connoisseur, this approachable course will give you the knowledge, tasting skills, and
vocabulary to enjoy wine more fully—and choose it more confidently.

Throughout this 4-week course, you will explore the world’s primary grape varieties and
discover the many styles of white, rosé, red, and sparkling wines. We will break down
the basics of viticulture and winemaking so you can understand how grapes, regions,
and production choices shape the flavors, aromas, body, and texture in every glass. You
will also learn what makes the major wine-producing countries distinctive and how to
recognize key differences among grape varieties and wine styles.

Each session includes guided tasting practice, from visual assessment through aroma,
flavor, structure, and finish, helping you evaluate wine and learn why you like or dislike
different wines. Durin the 4 weeks, we will taste 20–25 wines from around the world,
making this class both educational and delicious. By the end, you will feel more
comfortable ordering, buying, discussing, and enjoying wine in any setting.

THIS EVENT IS 21  Students will be required to show a government ID to the instructor
upon arriving at the first session.

title: Building Your Financial Roadmap: A Financial Wellness Series
location: Montclair Bellevue Ave Branch - First Floor, Montclair Bellevue Avenue Branch
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Take control of your financial future with this four-part financial wellness workshop series designed to help you build a stronger foundation for making informed money decisions. Each workshop focuses on a practical aspect of financial wellness, from understanding how money grows and creating a plan for where your money should go, to preparing your family and planning for retirement.

Whether you're just getting started, looking to strengthen your financial habits, or preparing for the future, you'll gain practical knowledge, useful tools, and actionable strategies you can apply to your own financial life.

Each week we'll answer one important question about your financial future:


	
	How does money grow?
	



	
	Where should my money go first?
	



	
	How do I prepare my family for the future?
	



	
	How do I prepare myself for retirement?
	


Whether you attend one workshop or the entire series, you'll leave with practical knowledge and actionable steps to help you make informed financial decisions.

These workshops are for educational purposes only and are intended to provide general financial education. They should not be considered individualized financial, legal, tax, or investment advice.

title: Home Repair Essentials
location: Montclair - Montclair High School, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Learn the fundamentals of home repair in this practical, hands-on workshop taught by Robert Haas, instructor of the popular Woodworking 101 and Advanced Woodworking classes. Held at Montclair High School, this course gives participants a behind-the-walls look at how common home features are built and maintained.

During the class, instructor Rob Haas will construct two demonstration walls that include doors and a window, showing how these elements are installed and how typical wall structures are assembled. Participants will also learn how traditional double-hung windows operate and how they can be repaired, including basic glass pane replacement.

The workshop will also introduce the basics of residential wiring, demonstrating how outlets and lighting are installed and connected. Throughout the session, Robert will answer questions and offer guidance on a wide range of home repair topics.

Whether you're a homeowner looking to handle basic repairs yourself or simply curious about how things in your home work, this class provides practical knowledge you can use right away.

title: Fall Symposium: Reclaiming the Narrative
description:
In celebration of Archives Month, University Libraries will highlight how primary source materials can bring marginalized stories to the center of education, advocacy, and community engagement. Dr. Melissa Benbow Flowers, Scholar‑in‑Residence at Sprague Library (2025–2026), in collaboration with Bloomfield College, will host a symposium exploring how working‑class histories and undertold stories in New Jersey are researched, interpreted, and shared with the public. The program will bring together scholars, students, museum professionals, and public historians whose work focuses on labor, domestic work, immigration, race, and community change—particularly as these histories are communicated through museums, historic sites, archives, and public‑facing scholarship. Registration is free and open to students, faculty, staff, and members of the public—but limited! Registration closes September 18.
Register now for in-person attendance.
 
You can also attend virtually!

title: Courage, Choice, and What Comes Next with Dystopian Icon Veronica Roth
description:
A single choice can transform your destiny. Join us for an online conversation with #1 New York Times bestselling author Veronica Roth as we celebrate the enduring legacy of her Divergent series, one of the most iconic young adult series of a generation, and get an exclusive sneak peek into her highly anticipated upcoming novel, The Sixth Faction!

Fifteen years after readers first stepped into dystopian Chicago alongside Tris Prior, the Divergent universe continues to captivate readers with its unflinching exploration of identity, courage, and sacrifice. And in the alternate universe of The Sixth Faction, we revisit familiar characters in a completely new way… 

Beatrice Prior stands on the brink of a decision every person in her world must make: five factions, five futures, five lives.

She has a plan: she’s going to make the bravest choice and leave Abnegation to join Dauntless, even though it means abandoning her family.

But when tragedy strikes at her choosing ceremony, everything changes—her world, her plans, even Beatrice herself.

title: Essex Legislative Breakfast
location: Wilshire Grand Hotel, 350 Pleasant Valley Way, West Orange, NJ, 07052, United States
description:
The Essex County Mental Health & Addiction Coalition will host their 26th Annual Legislative Breakfast, providing a forum for community members and policymakers to address mental health developments. 
The Annual Legislative Breakfast represents an opportunity to initiate dialog with state, county and local representatives regarding issues of concern to the mental health community. It also serves as a vehicle for elected officials to share their positions with us on legislative matters that have the potential to impact individuals and families whose lives are affected by mental illnesses and/or behavioral disorders. 
By using the Annual Legislative Breakfast as a forum for speaking out on behalf of our society’s most vulnerable citizens, the Essex and Morris County Mental Health Coalition is committed to bringing about meaningful and lasting change within the mental health system. description:
Let's Walk!!
JOIN US FOR A WALK. WE WALK AT A MODERATE PACE ON UNPAVED PATHS.

location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
The Space We Made
Opening Reception 
Before The Space moves to its new home, we’re taking a look back and celebrating US!  Everyone who has walked through the door over the last 3 years has helped make The Space what it is.  You’ve lent your support, energy, and hearts to this cause.  You came together to explore something new, shared your art and ideas, witnessed creativity in action, made space for one another, bonded with new friends, and all with laughter, love and authenticity.  That was and always will be the invitation of The Space:  to come share, explore and witness the creative spirit.   
This last exhibit in this location take a look back at all the shows, the people, and the nights that filled this room. The Space We Made is a photo exhibit of everyone and everything that’s happened here, and the opening reception is a PARTY!! 
Friday, October 2 · 5–8 PM 
Free and open to all, but our fundraising drive has kicked off so donations along with your RSVP would go a long way to keeping The Space alive. 
We also welcome BYOB drinks and snacks to share.  We are all in this together! 
Help us send this room off right! 
RSVP encouraged so we know how many people to expect. 
If you have photos of good times and memories at The Space, we would love to get them in!  Email them to he***@************rt.com. We will keep adding to the exhibit, and more photos will be taken here over the next few weeks that we can print and add to the wall.  Its a participatory exhibit that will be up for several weeks.

description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: LINES TO LOVE: Screen-Free Afternoon with Your Child
location: The Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, loft #2, Montclair, NJ, 07042, United States
description:
Lines to Love:  A Creative Space for You & Your Child.
Led by Leo A. Sante
Remember what it felt like to simply be together with the child you love?

No screens, no rush, no expectations.

Just being side by side, doodling, making up stories, letting your imaginations wander wherever they wanted to go. 
Lines to Love brings you back to that space. 
Using a simple roll of paper and a few drawing materials, you and your child will be guided into a playful world of co-creation. 
Together, you’ll follow lines, add to each other’s doodles, build whimsical stories, and let the drawing become a pathway to imagination. 
Lines to Love is inspired by a cherished ritual between a father, Leo, and his young son, Lucas.  Back when Lucas was little, Leo would just roll out paper and two pens. Together they’d spend hours just doodling, creating, and enjoying the precious time together. Both Leo and Lucas cherish those drawings and those moments to this day. 
This is a free flowing togetherness workshop. It’s a rare chance to share precious, screen-free time. To explore, wonder, laugh, doodle quietly. To create something beautiful side by side. 
No artistic skills necessary. Just bring your open hearts.
All materials will be provided. 
You’ll leave with unforgettable memories and a creation you’ll both cherish all your lives. 

Ticket is for an adult + 1 child. The event is structured for 1:1 time.
Additional members of a family are welcome
Each child should be joined by an adult.
All materials will be provided.
All phones will be off and set aside for the duration of the session.
Space is limited to 15 pairs, so we recommend you reserve early.

title: Jersey Central Farewell Summer Shore Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this point to point hike in the north NJ shore region.
The theme of this one is of course the end of Summer, but also the historic Central Railroad of New Jersey.
The CNJ served a lot of shore points, and it's always fun to visit them on the hikes. So, for this one, we will focus on some of these rights of ways, including ones on the beach.
After meeting at the end point. Lot C at Sandy Hook, we will shuttle with as few vehicles as possible to a point south of Red Bank where there was a junction with the New York and Long Branch line.
The CNJ had a line to the east from here, which served Port Monmouth and continued east to a junction with the Seashore Branch.
We will trace this as closely as possible. Some bits of it are now trail, but they are very short. Some bits are now parking lots, gas lines, or roads. The route will take us through the raceway area, and then out toward the shore line.
We'll continue north following the rail grade as closely as possible, and eventually it turns into a walkway along the sea wall.
We'll continue on that walkway to the north to Sandy Hook, and probably at some point head to the water for a couple of breaks before the end.
There will be places for food and drinks along the way.
If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
**TRAIL WORK (which was canceled Sept. 13th due to steady rain) will continue rerouting the Hogenauer Trail** (we are making progress!) up the slope and away from recently installed property fences. **Meet At:** Dog Park/ Wildflower Preserve, 11 Bear Lane, Maplewood. From there, we will walk to Crater View on Crest drive and then to the Hogenauer trail work site. (Note: While we normally meet the first Sudnay of each month, this volunteer day was shifted after the Labor Day weekend.)

Trail work is physically challenging but very satisfying as we use hand tools to build and repair trails. Participants must be 15+ years. Those younger than 18 must be accompanied by an adult. Participants **should wear long pants** due to [ticks](https://www.somocon.org/?page_id=193928&fb) and thron bushes and sturdy shoes, and bring gloves (though backup gloves will be available). Tools, water, and a snack will be provided. (Registration is not required though if you sign up on Meetup, it helps us know how many tools to bring.) Only heavy, steady rain cancels.

title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Sundays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: Everything Book Club, "The Ministry of Time" by Kaliene Bradley
location: Montclair Main - Teen Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
NEW LOCATION: Teen Room on first floor. An instant New York Times bestseller. In the near future, a new government ministry is exploring time travel. Our heroine gets a highly paid job assisting and monitoring the time travel expat known as “1847” or Commander Graham Gore. As far as history is concerned, Commander Gore died on a doomed 1845 expedition to the Arctic, so he’s a little disoriented by living with an unmarried woman who regularly shows her calves, uses outlandish devices such as “washing machines” and “Spotify,” and talks about “the collapse of the British Empire.”  This witty, sexy, genre-bending debut novel will tug your heartstrings, make you laugh, and ultimately make you think.

"A hilarious yet poignant take on dislocation, loss, and oddball community . . .  A twisty plotline that incorporates plenty of John le Carré and Mick Herron spy-craft references . . .  with the silly, incisive, and spot-on comedy of Douglas Adams."—The Boston Globe

Kaliane Bradley is a British-Cambodian writer and editor based in London. Her short fiction has appeared in Somesuch Stories, The Willowherb Review, Electric Literature, Catapult, and Extra Teeth, among others. She was the winner of the 2022 Harper’s Bazaar Short Story Prize and the 2022 V.S. Pritchett Short Story Prize.

title: Pasta with a Twist: A Fresh Take on Italian Classics with Food Network Star Joe Sasto
description:
It’s time to ditch the same boring recipes and bring big, playful creativity back into your kitchen! Join us for an online conversation with Top Chef finalist and Food Network star Joe Sasto as we explore his hit national bestselling cookbook, Breaking the Rules: A Fresh Take on Italian Classics. 

Whether you are a novice cook looking to build your kitchen confidence or an experienced chef eager to expand your culinary repertoire, Joe’s approachable philosophy will change how you view everyday ingredients. We will dive deep into his vibrant world of handcrafted pasta, step-by-step rolling techniques, and unexpected flavor profiles. 

From foundational family favorites like his mom’s red sauce to daring, crave-worthy creations like Corn Cacio e Pepe, Marinated Tomato “Amatriciana,” and Pesto Pinwheel Pull-Apart Bread, this conversation is an open invitation to trust your culinary instincts and cook with absolute freedom.

Register today and learn how to make cooking fun again!

 

About the Author: 

Celebrity chef Joe Sasto found his love for cooking and appetite for Italian classics as a child at his mother's side. When the COVID-19 pandemic hit in March 2020, he pivoted his career by teaching virtual pasta-making classes.

With more than half a billion likes and countless viral social media videos, Sasto has become a recurring judge and chef personality across multiple shows on the Food Network. He's also competed and appeared on Food Network shows such as Guy Fieri's Tournament of Champions, Guy's Grocery Games, and Chopped, as well as Bravo's Top Chef and Top Chef All-stars.

In 2022, Sasto made the Food Network's first-ever "Hot List." Aside from his career as a chef, Sasto has developed a high-end customizable pasta and pizza tool line, and he is the creator of Tantos, the first puffed pasta chip, and a gourmet frozen ravioli brand, Ripi. His first cookbook, Breaking the Rules – a fresh take on Italian classics, was published in October 2025. He lives in Chicago and enjoys spending time with his pup, Tito, and his wife, Kait.

title: The American Experiment ;Migration, Identity, and the American Nation
description:
Join President Koppell for his first lecture in the American Experiment series, where he will discuss migration, identity, and the American nation.
Migration has been central to the American experience from the nation’s earliest history to the present. It has shaped the country’s population, economy, politics, culture, and understanding of national identity, while also generating recurring debates over citizenship, belonging, borders, assimilation, and exclusion. This lecture examines how migration, including internal and forced migration, has influenced the development of the United States and how Americans have defined who belongs within the national community. It considers the tensions between the country’s long-standing identity as a nation of immigrants and its equally significant history of restriction, exclusion, and contested membership. The discussion will explore how race, ethnicity, religion, class, and demographic change have shaped immigration policy and public attitudes, while placing contemporary debates over borders, citizenship, birthright citizenship, integration, and national identity within a broader historical and constitutional context. At its center is an enduring question for American democracy: How should a nation shaped by migration define membership, belonging, and shared identity in a period of rapid global and demographic change?

title: Breaking the Silence: Understanding Depression, Suicide, and the Power of Connection
description:
Presentation by Dr. Jason Dean and Dr. Rae Dumont

Depression is often misunderstood, accompanied with shame, secrecy or blame. So is suicide. The impact a loss by suicide has on friends and family is enormous. Without open conversations, people often feel alone as they carry the memory and question themselves about what they might have done to help. 

This presentation, in the context of a rising incidence of depression, anxiety and suicide, aims to offer understanding and compassion for people who struggle with mental illness. It  offers insights and comfort to those who have loved a person with depression, and tried to help. 

 

There will be ample time for discussion and for questions.

 

Rae Dumont, MD, LMFT, is both a pediatrician and a family therapist. While she practiced and taught at Harvard Medical School, she focused on the impact of one person's illness through the entire family, and on the interconnection between mental and physical health. 

In her family therapy practice, she helped people navigate difficulties by collaborating, rather than becoming divided. 

She is also a mother, a widow, and a friend to many. She now turns her experiences into words that speak of resilience, and the flawed road toward becoming good enough. In her fiction, she finds a personal, intimate voice, which connects emotionally with her readers’ humanity.

In the Shadow of Silence, (2-17-2026) is a novel about love, family life, and depression. She hopes for it to bring insight and comfort to her readers. 

 

Jason Dean, MD is a child and adult psychiatrist and founder of The Center for Developmental Psychiatry, a group practice in Teaneck, NJ. He is also a Clinical Instructor at Yale School of Medicine.

In his clinical work, he has worked to integrate a biological, medical view of psychiatry with a psychological perspective. Dr. Dean hopes to augment the discussion with insight gained from his clinical experience and training, as well as his work with families of individuals struggling with depression.

title: Wine Confidence 101
location: Montclair - Cornerstone Montclair, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Build your wine confidence in just four weeks. Whether you are new to wine or already a
connoisseur, this approachable course will give you the knowledge, tasting skills, and
vocabulary to enjoy wine more fully—and choose it more confidently.

Throughout this 4-week course, you will explore the world’s primary grape varieties and
discover the many styles of white, rosé, red, and sparkling wines. We will break down
the basics of viticulture and winemaking so you can understand how grapes, regions,
and production choices shape the flavors, aromas, body, and texture in every glass. You
will also learn what makes the major wine-producing countries distinctive and how to
recognize key differences among grape varieties and wine styles.

Each session includes guided tasting practice, from visual assessment through aroma,
flavor, structure, and finish, helping you evaluate wine and learn why you like or dislike
different wines. Durin the 4 weeks, we will taste 20–25 wines from around the world,
making this class both educational and delicious. By the end, you will feel more
comfortable ordering, buying, discussing, and enjoying wine in any setting.

THIS EVENT IS 21  Students will be required to show a government ID to the instructor
upon arriving at the first session.

title: Home Repair Essentials
location: Montclair - Montclair High School, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Learn the fundamentals of home repair in this practical, hands-on workshop taught by Robert Haas, instructor of the popular Woodworking 101 and Advanced Woodworking classes. Held at Montclair High School, this course gives participants a behind-the-walls look at how common home features are built and maintained.

During the class, instructor Rob Haas will construct two demonstration walls that include doors and a window, showing how these elements are installed and how typical wall structures are assembled. Participants will also learn how traditional double-hung windows operate and how they can be repaired, including basic glass pane replacement.

The workshop will also introduce the basics of residential wiring, demonstrating how outlets and lighting are installed and connected. Throughout the session, Robert will answer questions and offer guidance on a wide range of home repair topics.

Whether you're a homeowner looking to handle basic repairs yourself or simply curious about how things in your home work, this class provides practical knowledge you can use right away.

title: Everything Book Club, "The Ministry of Time" by Kaliene Bradley, Session 2
location: Montclair Main - Tower Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
An instant New York Times bestseller. In the near future, a new government ministry is exploring time travel. Our heroine gets a highly paid job assisting and monitoring the time travel expat known as “1847” or Commander Graham Gore. As far as history is concerned, Commander Gore died on a doomed 1845 expedition to the Arctic, so he’s a little disoriented by living with an unmarried woman who regularly shows her calves, uses outlandish devices such as “washing machines” and “Spotify,” and talks about “the collapse of the British Empire.”  This witty, sexy, genre-bending debut novel will tug your heartstrings, make you laugh, and ultimately make you think.

"A hilarious yet poignant take on dislocation, loss, and oddball community . . .  A twisty plotline that incorporates plenty of John le Carré and Mick Herron spy-craft references . . .  with the silly, incisive, and spot-on comedy of Douglas Adams."—The Boston Globe

Kaliane Bradley is a British-Cambodian writer and editor based in London. Her short fiction has appeared in Somesuch Stories, The Willowherb Review, Electric Literature, Catapult, and Extra Teeth, among others. She was the winner of the 2022 Harper’s Bazaar Short Story Prize and the 2022 V.S. Pritchett Short Story Prize.

title: Art in Flight: Reinventing Postmodernism with Smithsonian Curator Carolyn Russo
description:
Join us for a captivating online conversation with acclaimed author and Smithsonian curator Carolyn Russo as we dive into her fascinating book, The Ascent of Rauschenberg. Explore the towering legacy, unexpected inspirations, and creative heights of one of America's most influential artistic icons.

Most famous for his groundbreaking "Combines"—painting and sculpture hybrids that often incorporated everyday objects—American artist Robert Rauschenberg (1925-2008) created within a range of mediums, including collage, performance, photography, and printmaking. But a connective tissue through it all was his fascination with flight. The Ascent of Rauschenberg explores the flight motif across his work, spanning birds, insects, aviation, spaceflight, sensory experiences, and metaphors for his own life.

More than 150 images reveal the vibrant scope of his work, from lithographs inspired by the Apollo 11 launch that NASA invited him to witness and document, to a Combine featuring a taxidermied eagle that evokes Roman mythology. Nine accompanying essays reflect on his many flight themes and subtleties that might otherwise be overlooked. The book also includes archival photographs and personal papers from the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation.

Register now for the chance to view art history through the unique prism of flight. 

About the Author:

Carolyn Russo is curator of the art collection at the Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum. She has lectured internationally on the subject of art and flight and is the author of several publications including The Ascent of Rauschenberg: Reinventing the Art of Flight, Art of the Airport Tower, In Plane View: Abstractions of Flight, and Women and Flight: Portraits of Contemporary Women Pilots.

title: Weekly Food Recovery Initiative
description:
Join our weekly Food Recovery events, where dedicated volunteers and members gather to make a difference in our community. Each week, participants help collect perfectly good leftover food from Gourmet Dining and transport it to Blanton. There, the food is repackaged into individual microwavable containers and stocked in the food pantry, providing meals for those in need throughout the week. 
To Participate: RSVP to attend the event each week. Meet in Blanton Hall Residence Hall Kitchenette in the Communal Area (Tell them you are working with Food Recovery), Sign in via Event Pass and your set!
Requirements:

Volunteers must be Food Safe Certified to participate.
Complete the certification by following the step-by-step instructions provided in this link.
Once certified, email your certification to foodrecoverynetwork@sgamsu.org to confirm your eligibility to participate.

Your involvement helps reduce food waste and insecurity while supporting individuals in our community who are in need. We look forward to your participation!*Please Note: This event end time is dependent on the amount of food given. You can estimate for max of hour and a half for recoveries.

title: Mending with Hands, Hearts, and Minds
Faculty Concert: Chris Opperman, Composition
description:
Faculty Concert: Chris Opperman, Composition
Dr. Chris Opperman wields a special array of expertise. He is a composer of wildly original music, a top orchestrator and arranger, a dedicated and visionary educator, and a trusted advisor for an incredible cross-section of the music industry.
Since starting his Purple Cow Records label in 1998, Dr. Opperman has released six prior albums including 2001’s Klavierstücke, his first solo piano album, and 2010’s The Lionheart, an orchestral rock album. He has also released three EP’s including 2022’s Four Improvisations which feature studio-manipulated piano works, and two singles including “And If You Know” featuring Robert Martin.
With Arnie & Eric Roth of AWR Music, Dr. Opperman has worked on several national and international orchestral and chamber music tours including Distant Worlds: music from FINAL FANTASY, A New World: intimate music from FINAL FANTASY, the FINAL FANTASY VII Remake Orchestra World Tour, The Beach Boys Holiday Vibrations Orchestra Tour, several Mannheim Steamroller Christmas tours, and Undertale LIVE. Dr. Opperman’s arrangements with AWR and others have been performed by renowned and accomplished orchestras at premiere venues which include Carnegie Hall, the Royal Albert Hall, the Tokyo International Forum, and more.
Along with much other music, Opperman played piano on two of Steve Vai’s Grammy-nominated compositions, “Lotus Feet” from Real Illusions: Reflections and “The Attitude Song” from Sound Theories, Vols. I and II, both with the Metropole Orkest. He’s also performed with virtuoso multi-instrumentalist Mike Keneally, Indian classical music masters L. Shankar (a.k.a. Shenkar) and Zakir Hussein, former Duran Duran/Missing Persons guitarist Warren Cuccurullo, and many others.
Dr. Opperman holds a Ph. D. In Music Composition and has taught undergraduate and graduate level courses on music theory and composition, popular and classical music history, music technology, and the music industry.
Learn more about Chris Opperman

Hosted by: The College of the Arts

description:
Coordinating with the release of the dam in the Lehigh River, this whitewater rafting trip is sure to be a blast. Perfect for all skill levels. This is a great way to GET YOUR FEET WET! 
 
How do I Sign-up?

Register here, or in the Student Recreation Center's main office, or over the phone (973-655-3340).
Cost for Students  $20 

 
Where and when?

Saturday, October 10, 2026
7:00am – 7:00pm
Begins at Student Recreation Center

 
What to bring: Lunch, water, snacks, towel, a change of clothes and sandals with a heel strap, old sneakers, or water shoes. Flip-flops or slides are not allowed. For warmer days, wear a swim suit or quick-drying shorts/shirt; for cooler days, bring extra layers, but no cotton. Wetsuits are included for those that want them.Half/full wetsuits can be rented from the organization. Half is $6, full is $12, jacket is $4.

description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Pollinator Meadow activities will focus on pathway installation and invasive species sweep and removal. Work is strenuous to moderate. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can start promptly at 10 am.

Please dress appropriately! Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots. please no bug spray. Wear sunscreen and a hat. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

title: Cookbook Swap & Baked Goods Tasting
description:
Join us for another Cookbook Swap!

Cookbook Swap: 10:30 AM–1:30 PM | Café Area
Baked Goods Tasting: 12:00–1:30 PM | Auditorium

Bring your gently used cookbooks and exchange them 1-for-1 with fellow culinary enthusiasts. Maximum of 5 books.


	
	Drop off your cookbooks at the library in advance, prior to October 10.
	
	On the day of the event, for every cookbook you’ve donated, you’ll get to choose a new one to take home!


And this time, we’re adding something delicious! You can bring a homemade baked good for fellow cookbook lovers to sample and enjoy. Please bring your baked good ready to serve—there will be no heating, reheating, or cooking of food at the event. Bringing a baked good is completely optional—you’re welcome to attend the cookbook swap and bake-off even if you don’t bring food.

If you plan to bring a baked good, please email adultprograms@montclairlibrary.org and let us know what you will be bringing. All baked goods must be nut-free.

Please note: Baked goods may contain other common allergens, and the library cannot guarantee an allergen-free environment or be responsible for allergic reactions or other food-related sensitivities. Please use your best judgment when sampling foods.

title: Finish Strong and Position Your Business for Growth
description:
Montclair Business Networking
Year-end has a way of sneaking up on business owners. You’re focused on finishing the year strong while budgets need attention, next year’s marketing plan is taking shape, staffing decisions are looming, and new growth goals are already on the table.
Before you start setting goals for 2027, there are some bigger questions worth asking:

* What drove your growth this year and where did you fall short?

* Does your team have the capacity and skills to support where you want to go?

* Are your marketing, financial, and operational plans working together toward the same goals?

Join us on October 13th and we’ll help you unpack it.
The panel discussion brings together experts in business growth, marketing, HR, and accounting to help you build a stronger foundation for the year ahead.
Topics include:

* 2026 Performance Review: What your financial results, marketing performance, and workforce health say about where your business stands.

* 2027 Growth Planning: Marketing, financial, and workforce decisions to make now as you set your goals for the new year.

* Execution Readiness: The people, processes, systems, and financial foundation you need in place to carry out your plan.

Who Should Attend?

* Business owners and entrepreneurs

* CEOs and senior leaders

* Sales and marketing leaders

* HR and people leaders

* Business development professionals

* Anyone responsible for helping their organization grow in 2027

Don’t wait until January to figure out what 2027 should look like. Use this session to take stock of where your business stands, identify what needs attention, and head into the new year ready to act.
Reserve your spot!

title: Crane's Mill:  The Story Behind the Name
location: West Caldwell - Community Meeting Room, West Caldwell Public Library
description:
Join local historian Bob Williams on Tuesday, October 13 at 6:30 p.m. at the West Caldwell Public Library for a fascinating look at the history of Crane’s Mill and its connection to West Caldwell.

The story has a personal connection for Williams. When he was just 15 years old, he purchased a collection of historic ledgers from Crane’s Sawmill in West Caldwell. By then, the mill had already been dismantled and moved to Allaire Village in South Jersey for reconstruction although it was never rebuilt. The mill’s foundation ruins remained in West Caldwell for years, becoming a favorite place for Williams to explore throughout his youth and into adulthood.

title: Open Book / Open Mind; Heather McGhee; "The Sum of Us." With Michelle Alexander.
location: Montclair - First Congregational Church of Montclair, Montclair Public Library
description:
What if we've been looking at opportunity in America all wrong? What if individual groups stopped trying to get a larger slice of the pie and worked together to create a bigger, better pie? 

Join the Montclair Public Library and Partners for Health Foundation for an inspiring conversation between Heather McGhee, an influential economic and public policy expert, and Michelle Alexander, a renowned civil rights lawyer and author. They'll be talking about "The Sum of Us: What Racism Costs Everyone and How We Can Prosper Together," McGhee's landmark New York Times bestseller from 2021 about how overcoming racism helps everyone, not just people of color, and how to move beyond the zero-sum vision of American opportunity.  

After the discussion, there will be a Q&A period, followed by signing with Watchung Booksellers. 

Thanks to the generosity of Partners for Health Foundation, free copies of “The Sum of Us” will be available to the first 50 guests to enter (who have not already received books in the Library’s community read). 

Join our community read, Montclair Reads "The Sum of Us," between June and October to get ready for this exceptional evening. Thanks to the generosity of Partners for Health, we'll be giving away free books to book clubs while supplies last. Click here for more details and to find out about other supporting programs. 

The event will take place at the First Congregational Church of Montclair, 40 S. Fullerton Avenue. Doors open at 6:30 p.m. The event is free but registration is required.

Open Book / Open Mind is sponsored by Montclair Public Library Foundation, Watchung Booksellers, Anonymous Dr. Alex and Doris Malaspina, David and Mary Lee Jones, and our individual Underwriters. We are also grateful for the generous support of our in-kind sponsors, First Congregational Church of Montclair, The George, and Amanti Vino. To join our Open Book / Open Mind Underwriters, click here.

title: All In: The Fight for Democracy Film Screening & Civic Engagement Experience
description:
Democracy doesn't protect itself—it depends on informed, engaged citizens.
Join Civic and Voter Engagement, in collaboration with the African American Caucus, for a powerful screening of All In: The Fight for Democracy, the critically acclaimed documentary that examines the history and present-day reality of voter suppression in the United States. Featuring voting rights advocate Stacey Abrams, the film explores the historical barriers, systemic inequities, and ongoing challenges that continue to shape access to the ballot box and influence civic participation.
More than a documentary, this screening is an opportunity to deepen your understanding of the democratic process, reflect on the importance of protecting voting rights, and engage in meaningful dialogue about one of the most fundamental rights in our democracy.
Following the screening, participants are invited to stay for a facilitated discussion exploring the themes of the film, the significance of voting rights in today's political landscape, and the role each of us can play in strengthening our democracy through civic engagement. Whether you're new to these conversations or actively engaged in public life, this discussion offers a welcoming space to learn from one another, share perspectives, and consider how informed civic participation can create positive change.
Join us for:

A screening of the award-winning documentary All In: The Fight for Democracy
A facilitated discussion on the film's relevance to today's political climate
Meaningful conversation with fellow students, faculty, and staff
Free food and refreshments
Civic-themed giveaways
Resources to help you stay informed and engaged

This event is open to all students, faculty, and staff. Come for the film, stay for the conversation, and leave with a deeper understanding of the importance of civic participation and the power of every voice.
Good film. Great conversation. Free food. Giveaways. One important conversation about the future of our democracy.

title: New Jersey's 44th Annual Law School Day
description:
Are you thinking about applying to law school? Join us for our 44th Annual NJ Law School Day at Montclair State University! All NJ college students and alumni who are interested in applying to law school are welcome to attend!
At NJ Law School Day, you can speak with law school representatives from NJ, NY, and across the U.S. about what their programs have to offer and how you can prepare to be a strong law school candidate.  Whether you are new to the idea of applying to law school or preparing to apply this fall, this event is a great opportunity to learn and connect.

 
What to Expect from Law School Day:
1pm - 2pm - Law School Panel Discussion
- For this session, you will hear from a panel of law school representatives about what they look for when reviewing law school applications and how to become a strong law school candidate.
 
2 - 4pm - The Law School Fair
- This is your chance to meet face-to- face with law school representatives from NJ, NY, PA, MA and across the U.S., and ask questions about applying to law school!
- The list of law schools attending is growing! Current law schools attending include: American, Fordham, Villanova, Ohio State, Seton Hall, Rutgers, Drexel, Penn State, Pace, Syracuse, Cardozo, Utah, Maryland, West Virginia, Richmond, Pittsburgh, and many, many more.  
- You can see the full list of law schools attending once you RSVP on Handshake on or after September 1, 2026
 
3:30 - 4:30 PM - Speed Mentoring: Pathways to Public Service
- After learning what it takes to get into law school, stick around to connect directly with professionals who are doing the work.  
- Through fast-paced, small-group rotating conversations, you’ll discover real-world career paths, and get honest insights into public interest and public service work. Come listen, ask questions, grab a snack, and make connections that can kickstart your legal, public interest, or public service career.
 
How to Be Prepared for Law School Day:

Be ready to share information about you, your interests, and your goals!
Write down the questions you have about law schools and the process of applying to law school
Bring something to take notes
Dress to impress!  Business attire is recommended
Registration for Law School Day will open on September 1, 2026 on Handshake
Questions? Need law school advice? Email Chrysten Colacicco, Pre-Law Program Coordinator at MSU, at colaciccoc@montclair.edu

title: Women and Money Roundtable - How to Make Sense of Today's Financial Markets
description:
A virtual, lively, and informative discussion on today’s financial markets and how they might fit into your portfolio. 


Julia Strayer and Liz Maccarone will lead a lively and informative discussion on today’s financial markets and how they might fit into your portfolio.

This is a virtual program that takes place over Zoom. As the date approaches, you will receive an email with the Zoom link.

About the Presenters

Julia Strayer, CPWA®, CIMA®, CRPC® Senior Vice President, Wealth Management Advisor.  Prior to joining Merrill Lynch Wealth Management in 2000, Julia was a vice president and private banker for BankBoston’s Private Bank for 7 years, responsible for asset management and trust services. Previously, Julia worked in marketing for 9 years with Merrill. Julia has a BA from Ohio State University and an MBA from New York University’s Stern School of Business. Julia has appeared on the CNBC show “Power Lunch,” CBS “This Morning,” WGCH’s “Women in Business,” in addition to featured articles in USA Today.

Liz Maccarone, CRPC® Senior Financial Advisor.  Liz joined Merrill Lynch Wealth Management in 2012. Liz works closely with high-net-worth individuals and their families to create personalized and comprehensive strategies that support their goals, including investment management, retirement planning, liability management, and multigenerational planning. Liz values the importance of establishing and cultivating relationships with families including the next generation. Liz graduated from Fairfield University with a dual bachelor’s degree in Finance and Marketing. She began her career working at a boutique investment firm as a Business Development Associate, specializing in commodities and futures trading.

title: Wine Confidence 101
location: Montclair - Cornerstone Montclair, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Build your wine confidence in just four weeks. Whether you are new to wine or already a
connoisseur, this approachable course will give you the knowledge, tasting skills, and
vocabulary to enjoy wine more fully—and choose it more confidently.

Throughout this 4-week course, you will explore the world’s primary grape varieties and
discover the many styles of white, rosé, red, and sparkling wines. We will break down
the basics of viticulture and winemaking so you can understand how grapes, regions,
and production choices shape the flavors, aromas, body, and texture in every glass. You
will also learn what makes the major wine-producing countries distinctive and how to
recognize key differences among grape varieties and wine styles.

Each session includes guided tasting practice, from visual assessment through aroma,
flavor, structure, and finish, helping you evaluate wine and learn why you like or dislike
different wines. Durin the 4 weeks, we will taste 20–25 wines from around the world,
making this class both educational and delicious. By the end, you will feel more
comfortable ordering, buying, discussing, and enjoying wine in any setting.

THIS EVENT IS 21  Students will be required to show a government ID to the instructor

title: Building Your Financial Roadmap: A Financial Wellness Series
location: Montclair Bellevue Ave Branch - First Floor, Montclair Bellevue Avenue Branch
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Take control of your financial future with this four-part financial wellness workshop series designed to help you build a stronger foundation for making informed money decisions. Each workshop focuses on a practical aspect of financial wellness, from understanding how money grows and creating a plan for where your money should go, to preparing your family and planning for retirement.

Whether you're just getting started, looking to strengthen your financial habits, or preparing for the future, you'll gain practical knowledge, useful tools, and actionable strategies you can apply to your own financial life.

Each week we'll answer one important question about your financial future:


	
	How does money grow?
	



	
	Where should my money go first?
	



	
	How do I prepare my family for the future?
	



	
	How do I prepare myself for retirement?
	


Whether you attend one workshop or the entire series, you'll leave with practical knowledge and actionable steps to help you make informed financial decisions.

These workshops are for educational purposes only and are intended to provide general financial education. They should not be considered individualized financial, legal, tax, or investment advice.

title: Home Repair Essentials
location: Montclair - Montclair High School, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Learn the fundamentals of home repair in this practical, hands-on workshop taught by Robert Haas, instructor of the popular Woodworking 101 and Advanced Woodworking classes. Held at Montclair High School, this course gives participants a behind-the-walls look at how common home features are built and maintained.

During the class, instructor Rob Haas will construct two demonstration walls that include doors and a window, showing how these elements are installed and how typical wall structures are assembled. Participants will also learn how traditional double-hung windows operate and how they can be repaired, including basic glass pane replacement.

The workshop will also introduce the basics of residential wiring, demonstrating how outlets and lighting are installed and connected. Throughout the session, Robert will answer questions and offer guidance on a wide range of home repair topics.

Whether you're a homeowner looking to handle basic repairs yourself or simply curious about how things in your home work, this class provides practical knowledge you can use right away.

title: ACC Teach-In: On the Origins of Modern US Foreign Interventionism & Iran
description:
Drawing inspiration from the mid-1960s anti-war movement, this teach-in will be an action-based educational forum concerning modern US foreign interventionism and its historical convergence with Iran during the Cold War. More specifically, it will focus on the rise of the postwar national security state and its first pivotal and consequential “win”: the 1953 Iranian coup d'état. It was the first "successful" overthrow of a democratically elected foreign leader by the CIA (and definitely not the last). It is a tale that is regularly expunged from conventional American history, yet it is vastly significant to both Iranian US history. This chapter elucidates, in part, why both nations find themselves where they are today. In addition, this teach-in will also highlight the determining role of big business, military keynesianism, and neocolonialism in shaping the confines of postwar U.S. foreign policy. This teach-in will conclude with a discussion on what this all means for the ongoing US-Israeli war against Iran, and what actionable acts can be done to end the conflict.

Hosted by: The Apple Core Community

title: Tea & Tarot - A bookclub style discussion group
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Monthly Gathering | Thursday, October 15th | 7:00 PM – 8:30 PM | The Space | $25 
Calling all tarot lovers, both new and seasoned!  Join us for an intimate way of exploring the cards. 
What could be better than a cozy evening of warm tea and deep conversation? Join us for Tea & Tarot with Gina Devine—a monthly, book club-style discussion group created to deepen our connection with the archetypes of the tarot through community and shared insight. 
Rather than a formal class, this is a casual meet-up where we treat the tarot as a living text. Based on the psychological insights of Carl Jung, we will explore the Major Arcana not just as fortune-telling tools, but as mirrors of our own lives, rituals, and transformations. 
The Experience 
Each month, we open a new gateway of creative and spiritual exploration. Our time together includes: 

Archetypal Deep Dives: We’ll focus on a specific theme or set of cards each session, discussing their symbolism and how they show up in our modern world.
Collaborative Readings: A chance to pull cards for one another in a supportive, low-pressure environment.
Ritual & Connection: We’ll sip tea, share stories, and find common ground in the mysteries of the deck.
Intuitive Growth: Whether you’ve been reading for decades or just bought your first deck, you’ll leave with a deeper understanding of the “BodyGraph” of the tarot.

What to Bring 
To make the most of our evening, please bring the following if you can: 

Your Tarot Deck: Any deck you feel connected to.  If you don’t have any we have some available here to use.
Your Favorite Mug: We’ll provide a selection of teas, and don’t worry if you don’t bring your mug – we have those too!
A Notebook: For capturing insights, spreads, and “aha” moments.

Investment: $25 
Stay Connected: Sign up for the Soul Centric Tarot Newsletter here. 
Spaces are limited to keep our discussion intimate and impactful. Reserve your spot today and join the circle. 
Cover art by Sophie Bryant Funnell 
______________________________ 

Your Guide Gina Devine
Instagram: @gina.devine 

Gina Devine is an esoteric artist, intuitive tarot reader, writer, educator and guide. 
She has provided thousands of readings for people all over the world, and leads both protection and tarot workshops. Her approach to guidance is loving, grounded and human. Although she also teaches traditional tarot classes, her tea and tarot discussion group was birthed from the knowing that people are more inclined to to be in tune with the archetypes of the cards and the messages they bring when they are allowed space to enjoy the tarot in a more casual setting – instead of forcefully trying to memorize them. The same way we find joy in discussing a book in community, the cards also call for us to convene together around them. Her approach is philosophical, therapeutic and creative, and she is on a mission to guide people toward unearthing a more intimate and honest relationship with their inner knowing through the art of divination. You can find her services and more at soulcentrictarot.com

title: Compagnie Hervé KOUBI: Sol Invictus
description:
Run Time: 75 minutes, no intermission. 
A jubilant ritual full of love and light from the acclaimed French-Algerian ensemble Compagnie Hervé KOUBI. Named after the “invincible sun” deity, Sol Invictus upholds love as the guarantor of peace, that despite fracture, communion emerges as humanity’s saving grace. A vivid celebration of solidarity and the bonds that unite us, in Sol Invictus the sun will emerge victorious. The score includes a composition by Swedish composer Mikael Karlsson, with excerpts by Steve Reich and digital composer Maxime Bodson. 
“The dancers of Compagnie Hervé KOUBI could be mistaken for gods.” (The New Yorker) 
About Compagnie Hervé KOUBI: Absolutely unique and utterly original, this fearless, powerful company reigns from France, Algeria, and beyond. Combining contemporary and urban dance movements, capoeira, and martial arts with powerful imagery and inspired choreography, the dancers defy gravity.

description:

title: Entrepreneurship Bootcamp
location: Bloomfield - Conference Room, Bloomfield Public Library
description:
*** This is a free program, but you must register to attend. 

email: reference@bloomfield.bccls.org

call: 973-566-6200 ext. 215 ***

Thinking about starting a business—or wondering what it takes to move your idea to the next level? This two-day introductory entrepreneurship bootcamp provides a practical overview of the key areas every new entrepreneur should understand.

Presented by Jesse Bryant, Certified Business Consultant with the Small Business Administration (SBA), SCORE, and Veterans Business Outreach Center (VBOC), the program will cover the fundamentals of building a business, including financing options, sales and marketing strategies, intellectual property, choosing the right legal entity, business planning, and incorporating AI into business operations. Participants will also learn about revenue-readiness software and discover support programs, resources, and organizations available to help entrepreneurs launch and grow.

This program is designed for aspiring entrepreneurs, new business owners, veterans, and anyone interested in learning more about the process of turning a business idea into a sustainable venture. No prior business experience is required.

title: NJ Code & Coffee - Newark Tech Week edition
description:
NJ Code & Coffee
Calling all New Jersey techies to the **NJ Code and Coffee** tech community meetup at the EqualSpace ES550 Tech & Innovation campus during Newark Tech Week!

Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal networking/co-working session for those in tech (and the tech-curious).
That includes operators, founders, and investors. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, software engineers, solution architects... **all are welcome!**

People of all skill and experience levels can attend, we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, and many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. It's entirely up to you!

Come grab a cup of coffee and meet new people, share stories, find collaborators, talk about everything tech, talk about everything NOT tech, take a break from job applications, get away from the computer screen, make connections, make conversation, **make friends!**

**Agenda:**
**2pm:** Doors open, networking starts
**2:30pm:** Intro circle
**3pm:** networking continues
**5pm:** event ends

**The Intro Circle**
**Near the beginning of the event (about 2:30 pm), we will do a standup in a circle:**
We first talk about organizer announcements, updates, and logistics. Then we go around the circle where each person says:

* your name and job title/ role in tech/ tech stack,
* What you can help others with,
* What you would like help with,
* Job opportunities you're hiring for OR announce that you are looking for one. If none, that's cool.

After the introduction circle, everything is self-organized.

**Community Discord - come hang out before and after!:**
[www.codeandcoffee.chat](www.codeandcoffee.chat)

**The Venue**
Equal Space is a premium share-space created with multicultural business owners in mind, =SPACE equips founders with resources, programming and a powerful network.

Headquartered in the City of Newark, their share-space provides resources for startups, coaching for tech companies, and a wealth of intellectuals to collaborate and build with. The next wave in enterprises is being born within their walls. Become a part of the story: [EqualSpace.co/](https://equalspace.co/)

description: On Sunday, October 18, we kick off our Stewardship Campaign. This is the time of year when we each recommit our time, talent, and treasure to the Holy Spirit Verona Community. This year’s theme "Plenty Good Room" is an opportunity to be reminded that there are "many rooms" in God's house, as the Gospel Writer of John tells us. How are you welcoming others to Holy Spirit Verona? title: Forest Regeneration Volunteer Workday
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
Forest Regeneration activities focus on the areas in and around the fenced 14-acre Forest and Wildflower Preserve located near the Dog Park on Bear Lane in the Reservation. On workdays, we focus on removing invasive plants like knotweed, garlic mustard and mugwort. Ages 12 to 15 are welcome with a parent or guardian present. Ages 15 and above require a signature by a parent or guardian on a [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi); teenagers cannot just be dropped off.

Please arrive 5 to 10 minutes early so we can hike into the Wildflower Preserve at 9 am sharp.

Please dress appropriately! There is some poison ivy on trails and in work areas. Wear long pants, long-sleeved shirt, closed-toe shoes or rain boots, bug spray, and layer as needed. We supply tools. If you have gloves, bring them or you can borrow a pair from us. Bring your own water.

You can download a copy of our [liability waiver](https://1drv.ms/b/c/d5fb9d3835660a78/IQCJO4IIj6GnQ6N4RuNC981xAYL2kFajs9_RL8f8V7NkhaM?e=5bd5oi) to print, sign and bring to the event.

We occasionally use photos of events in promotional materials and social media. By attending the event, I consent to photos of me being used in promotional materials or on social media.

For information, contact program co-coordinators Rich Rockwell and Tom Pollard at forestregen@[somocon.org](http://somocon.org/)

To see what's blooming in the Wildflower Preserve, check out our [Wildflower Preserve](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-conservancy-wildflower-preserve) project on iNaturalist. We also have [South Mountain Reservation](https://www.inaturalist.org/projects/south-mountain-reservation) project there, that captures observations from the entire reservation.

**Meet at the tool sheds at the Dog Park at 12 Bear Lane, Maplewood NJ**
**GPS:** 40.739791, -74.289181

title: Affordable College Solutions NOW ON ZOOM
description:
Register HERE

Join us for the special ZOOM presentation of the "Cracking the Code: Affordable College Solutions" seminar.  

It doesn't matter how old your kids are...now is the time to learn how to finance college!

This program will be presented by a nationally recognized Certified College Funding Specialist who has
been invited to speak to families and professionals by more than 65 organizations nationwide. She has also
provided continuing education to over 40,000 CPAs across the country on strategies to help make college
more affordable.
Designed for parents with children of all ages—from newborn through college—this engaging and informative
session addresses one of the most stressful financial challenges families face today: how to pay for college
without jeopardizing long-term financial goals and retirement. Even higher-income families with substantial
resources can feel overwhelmed by the tremendous cost of school and seek guidance to navigate the quickly
evolving college process to secure discounts and preserve their wealth.
A featured focus of the presentation is recent legislation often referred to as “The Big Beautiful Bill,” and
what it means for college savings, financial aid, and affordability. The presenter will explain these changes in a
clear, practical, and easy-to-understand way.
Participants will also learn about:
● How to secure a quality education without overpaying for college
● Understanding the financial aid landscape: FAFSA and CSS Profiles, need-based and merit-based aid,
athletic and private scholarships
● Student Aid Index (SAI): How it’s calculated and directly impacts your family’s financial aid eligibility
● Pros and Cons of Diverse College Savings Vehicles - a look at 529 plans as well as alternative savings
strategies and determining how to choose what’s right for your family
● How to reduce student loan debt and plan for repayment without sacrificing your family’s future
● Strategies to recapture out-of-pocket college expenses
● Positioning families to maximize college discounts: Practical strategies—even for higher-income
households—to unlock savings opportunities
Participants will gain valuable insights, expert guidance, and creative strategies to help make smarter college
funding decisions while protecting the ability to retire comfortably. This program is designed to simplify and
demystify the college funding process, empowering families to reduce costs and avoid unnecessary debt.
Whether your child was just born or is approaching college decisions, this program will provide clarity,
confidence, and practical guidance you can use right away.



PRESENTED BY: Jodi Bloom, MBA
Certified College Funding Specialist
Founder and College Planning Expert

title: Everything Book Club, "Kin" by Tayari Jones, Session 2
description:
An instant New York Times bestseller by the author of "An American Marriage." A selection for both Oprah's Book Club and The New York Times Book Review Book Club. 

Goes with the Open Book / Open Mind program with Tayari Jones about "Kin" the following week on Tuesday, September 15! Tickets cost $35 and include a signed copy of the book. (If for any reason you can't afford a ticket, come talk to me.)

We'll talk about Jones's conversation as well as "Kin," a poignant historical novel set in the civil rights era about two motherless childhood friends who take very different journeys: one to the storied HBCU Spellman College, the other to make her way in the world. 

TAYARI JONES is the author of four other novels, most recently the New York Times bestseller "An American Marriage," which was an Oprah’s Book Club selection and also appeared on Barack Obama’s summer reading list and his year-end roundup. It won the Women’s Prize for Fiction, the Aspen Words Literary Prize, and an NAACP Image Award and has been published in two dozen countries. Jones is the C.H. Candler Professor of English and Creative Writing at Emory University and lives in Atlanta.

	greetings
	personal information
	expressions of courtesy
	feelings
	asking for direction
	talk about needs and want
	where people are from.
	Alphabet
	Numbers/Days/date
	Colors
	Basic commands
	Some ar/er/ir  regular verbs
	Verb to be: ser/estar
	Verb to go: ir
	Verb Tener/Necesitar/Querer
	Ir   a
	Negation
	Subject pronouns/difference between Tú/Usted
	Gender and number of nouns/definite/indefinite articles
	Some adjectives including cuánto/a
	The expression “Hay”
	Basic geography, culture and food.

Held at Montclair High School, this course gives participants a behind-the-walls look at how common home features are built and maintained.

During the class, instructor Rob Haas will construct two demonstration walls that include doors and a window, showing how these elements are installed and how typical wall structures are assembled. Participants will also learn how traditional double-hung windows operate and how they can be repaired, including basic glass pane replacement.

The workshop will also introduce the basics of residential wiring, demonstrating how outlets and lighting are installed and connected. Throughout the session, Robert will answer questions and offer guidance on a wide range of home repair topics.

Whether you're a homeowner looking to handle basic repairs yourself or simply curious about how things in your home work, this class provides practical knowledge you can use right away.

title: Zoom: Successfully Navigating College Admissions
description:
Register HERE





We are offering this Zoom presentation to help families of high school juniors, sophomores, and freshmen better understand the college admissions process and how to successfully navigate today’s changing landscape.

 

The session will cover current college admissions trends and strategies, the evolving test optional environment, the importance of researching and visiting colleges to find the right fit, and key timelines and action steps that can make this fall productive while easing stress around the college admissions process.

 

We will also take a close look at the holistic admissions review process, including what admissions officers value when evaluating applicants and how students can develop a strong personal narrative that reflects their strengths, interests, character, and experiences.

 

Another focus will be on the role of community service and the growing importance of meaningful “passion projects.” We will discuss how students can turn their interests, values, and experiences into authentic activities that foster personal growth, demonstrate character, and show positive impact. Admissions officers place great emphasis on character, and thoughtful service can help students show initiative, empathy, and a genuine commitment to helping their communities.

 

This program is recommended for parents and their high school teens. It provides a clear and strategic overview of what students should prioritize this fall for a successful college admissions journey and how to approach the process with confidence and less stress.

 

The presentation will be led by Ron Feuchs and Jackie Tepper, partners at Stand Out For College, LLC (www.standoutforcollege.com).

title: Book Talk: From the Abuelas' Window by Nancy Burke
location: Montclair Main - Classroom, Montclair Public Library
description:
Join us for a book talk with author Nancy Burke about her book From the Abuelas' Window. The novel is currently being adapted for the musical stage!

About the book
It is Chile, 1974. Pinochet has taken over the presidential palace and the government far away in Santiago. The village school in a remote farming community has been closed and converted into a detention center for political prisoners. Maribel, a young girl in the village, is protected by her mother from the truth about her father who is among the prisoners but has been moved to an unknown place.

Three nosy old neighbors, the abuelas, love to peek out their window and watch Maribel and her sisters play innocent games in their mother's beautiful garden. They are rumored to have strange, magical powers, but stubborn and restless Maribel doesn't believe the rumors. She just wants her Papa, who she believes is visiting sick relatives, back so her mother doesn't depend on the abuelas for help.

A gift from the abuelas sets the story in motion and in a curiosity-driven moment, Maribel learns the truth about her father. The gift, an old red bicycle, takes her beyond the confines of her mother's garden and into the reality her mother can no longer keep from her.

Maribel responds by helping her mother bring food to the prisoners in her old school. She keeps a list of names of the innocent, hoping somewhere, someone is doing the same for her father.

The military comes in force to their village. Others are arrested, including Maribel's mother. The sisters discover a young girl, Sandra, hiding in their orchard. Her parents have been taken. Books are burned, songs are banned, but the village festival is held as usual, although under the watchful eye of the captain of the guard.

Maribel and her sisters take the power of love and magic, learned from the crafty old abuelas, into their own hands to change the course of fate for their family, their friends and a group of innocent strangers. Someone, somewhere, does the same for Papa.

About the Author
Nancy Burke is the author of Only the Women are Burning (2020), If I Could Paint the Moon Black (2014), From the Abuelas’ Window (2005) and a new short story collection, Death Cleaning and Other Units of Measure (2024). She holds an MFA in Fiction (Dramatic Writing concentration) from Rutgers’ University, Newark and a BA in Anthropology from Montclair State University. Her short stories have appeared in Pilgrim: A Journal of Catholic Experience, Meat for Tea: The Valley Review. At the Pool was a finalist for the J.F. Powers Award for Short Fiction at Dappled Things Literary Journal. Her screenplay adaptation of Only the Women are Burning won a Finalist recognition from the 2023 Boston Screenplay Competition. She is at work on a musical adaptation of From the Abuelas’ Window. Visit her Work in Progress page for info on this project. She teaches writing at New Jersey Institute of Technology and lives in Little Falls, NJ.

www.nancyburkestories.com

title: Ghosts, Grief, and Growing Up: YA Storytelling with Cherie Dimaline
description:
Step into the atmospheric and deeply moving world of storytelling with acclaimed Métis author Cherie Dimaline as we discuss her captivating body of work and her haunting Young Adult novel, Funeral Songs for Dying Girls.

Set in a cemetery shed where sixteen-year-old Winifred lives with her dad, Funeral Songs for Dying Girls follows a teen whose attempt to save her father's job leads to a fake ghost rumor—and accidentally summons a very real, opinionated spirit named Phil. Through this eerie yet heartwarming story, Dimaline crafts a haunting masterpiece about grief, survival, identity, and unexpected connections across the boundary of life and death. 

Beyond her graveyard-set YA novel, we will explore Dimaline’s expansive literary career—from the groundbreaking dystopian survival narrative of The Marrow Thieves and its sequel Hunting by Stars, to the dark, magic-infused folklore of her adult novels like Empire of Wild and VenCo.

Register today to participate in this spellbinding conversation!

 

About the Author: 

Cherie Dimaline is an internationally bestselling author. Her book The Marrow Thieves was named by TIME magazine, one of the Best YA Books of All Time and won the Governor General’s Award and the Kirkus Prize. Her novel Empire of Wild was an instant Canadian bestseller and is being adapted into a full opera for the Canadian Opera Company. Hunting By Stars was a 2022 American Indian Library Association Honor Book and her novel VENCO debuted at #1 on Canadian bestseller lists. Other titles include Funeral Songs for Dying Girls (AILA Honor Book, AURA Award winner, CRIME WRITERS Best Book, Bram Stoker Finalist) and Into the Bright Open (2024 Governor General’s Award Finalist).

Cherie lives in her Georgian Bay Métis Community and has written and produced for MARVEL, FX, HBO, Disney, and is currently adapting two major projects for AMC.

title: Writing the Body - A Writing Workshop for Women
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Writing the Body – A Writing Workshop for Women
What can poetry say about our bodies that ordinary language can’t? How can our bodily experiences open new paths for our writing? 
In this generative workshop for women and nonbinary writers, Barbara O’Dair – poet, writer, and cofounder of the Park St. Writers Series – leads the group through readings, discussion, and writing exercises, using prompts to reveal fresh language, unexpected stories, and adventurous forms, and drawing from subjects such as body image, sexuality, desire, gender, illness, health, and aging. 
After a short grounding exercise, we’ll read and discuss a few poems that use the body and bodily experience to create meaning and music. Then we’ll write short pieces from three or four prompts. Everyone is encouraged to read their work aloud, and if time allows, the poet can take a few questions about their piece from the group. 
After a five-minute break, the second half of the workshop is devoted to writing a poem or creative piece and reading it aloud — either within the group, or as a “test drive” for the open mic later that evening. 
A few of the prompts (we may not get to all of them): 

If Your Body Could Talk… What would it say? Write a monologue in which one part of your body finally gets a chance to speak.
The Inherited Body. Finish this sentence: “I inherited my [body/hair/teeth] from…” Your parent is a natural choice, but consider more surprising options too — neighborhood, gender, class.
Medical Chart. Write a list of notes about your body that might appear on a medical chart, from a doctor’s POV. Then write your version: what should we know about you and your body? What does your version tell us about you?
Your Body in Time. Meet your body at eight, 25, 48, and today (or, if you’re under 40, work out the right ages). Introduce your different bodies to each other. Maybe your 48-year-old body wants a word with your eight-year-old body. About what?

Writing the Body – A Writing Workshop for Women 
Saturday, October 24, 4:30 – 6:30, $44 – price includes admission to the open mic.   
Workshop participants will be invited to read their work at the Space for Words open mic for writers that will follow the workshop later the same evening at 8pm.  The first portion of the open mic will be for workshop participants, and the second half is open to all women and female identifying persons. 
Learn more about the open mic here. 
 
Barbara O’Dair is a poet, writer, and cofounder of the Park St. Writers Series based in Montclair, NJ.
